messages.summary:
## Objective
- Update the existing playable game: keep its long story chapters, improve the hero’s torso and give him a suit, add gliding, and have him encounter criminals and villains.

## Requirements
- Build on the existing game without asking clarifying questions.
- Retain the long chapters.

## Decisions
- Kept the existing story chapter text and added a second East End crime encounter with a boss.
- Added a sculpted armored suit and cape, plus a spacebar/on-screen glide control.

## Objective
- Improve the existing playable game while retaining its long story chapters; enhance the hero’s suit, add gliding, and introduce criminals and a villain encounter.

## Requirements
- Build on the existing game without asking clarifying questions.
- Keep the long chapters.

## Decisions
- Retained the existing story and added an East End crime encounter followed by a Black Mask-style boss fight.
- Added an armored suit, cape, and Space/on-screen glide controls.

## Work State
### Completed
- Updated the hero model with armor, cowl, emblem, belt, gauntlets, boots, and cape.
- Added glide controls and encounter HUD/objective updates.
- Fixed the duplicate `cape` declaration, renamed it `capeMesh`, updated cape visibility references, and removed Space’s accidental interaction trigger.
- Extracted the module script and passed `node --check` before the latest small input edit; `git diff --check` passed.
- Started the game in Playwright and advanced through the story into the cave scene.

### Active
- Validate cave equipment/elevator progression, combat, gliding, and the boss encounter in-browser.
- Review the final diff and rerun syntax and diff checks.

### Blocked
- Browser testing remains stuck on Alfred’s initial cave dialogue: repeated Enter presses and dispatched dialogue `pointerdown` events did not advance it.

## Next Move
1. Diagnose why the cave dialogue does not advance in Playwright, then test equipment/elevator progression, combat, gliding, and boss arrival.
2. Review `git diff` and run final syntax and diff checks.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: game implementation; only modified file.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted.
- Local server is running at `http://localhost:3002/`.
- Browser console reported a missing `/favicon.ico` (404) and GPU `ReadPixels` warnings.
- Screenshots were saved at `/tmp/opencode/game-check.jpg` and `/tmp/opencode/game-check-current.png`; the latest screenshot has not been meaningfully inspected.

## Objective
- Improve the existing playable game while retaining its long story chapters; enhance the hero’s suit, add gliding, and introduce criminals and a villain encounter.

## Requirements
- Build on the existing game without asking clarifying questions.
- Keep the long chapters.

## Decisions
- Retained the existing story and added an East End crime encounter followed by a Black Mask-style boss fight.
- Added an armored suit, cape, and Space/on-screen glide controls.
- Slowed enemy attacks and reduced combat damage after testing showed the player was overwhelmed quickly.

## Work State
### Completed
- Updated the hero model with armor, cowl, emblem, belt, gauntlets, boots, and cape.
- Added glide controls, encounter HUD/objective updates, and boss encounter logic.
- Fixed duplicate `cape` declaration and Space’s accidental interaction trigger.
- Removed the temporary `window.__gameDebug` helper.
- Updated guard damage text from `5` to `3` and fixed singular/plural gear objective text.
- Verified story dialogue can advance through all lines with Enter; its closing state is expected after the last line.
- `git diff --check` and `node --check` passed.

### Active
- Reload and test combat through the regular enemies and boss, including guard, dodge, attacks, and gliding.
- Verify the full cave-to-combat progression in-browser; recent scripted navigation did not successfully reach the elevator.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Reload and verify cave dialogue progression, collect equipment, and activate the elevator.
2. Test combat against regular enemies and Black Mask, including guard, dodge, attacks, and gliding; revisit damage/cooldowns if the player is still overwhelmed.
3. Re-run syntax and diff checks.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game implementation; only modified file.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted.
- Browser testing confirmed Enter advances the opening Alfred dialogue through all 11 lines and closes the dialogue afterward.
- Earlier combat test showed guard damage reports `BLOCKED — 3 DAMAGE`; a rapid unguarded attack sequence resulted in defeat before eliminating enemies.
- Earlier cave interaction testing reached the gear markers, but later scripted navigation stalled at the grapple gun and did not verify elevator activation.
- Earlier checks reported a missing `/favicon.ico` (404) and GPU `ReadPixels` warnings.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Improve the existing playable game while retaining its long story chapters; enhance the hero’s suit, add gliding, and introduce criminals and a villain encounter.

## Requirements
- Build on the existing game without asking clarifying questions.
- Keep the long chapters.

## Decisions
- Retained the existing story and added an East End crime encounter followed by a Black Mask-style boss fight.
- Added an armored suit, cape, and Space/on-screen glide controls.
- Slowed enemy attacks and reduced combat damage after testing showed the player was overwhelmed quickly.

## Work State
### Completed
- Updated the hero model with armor, cowl, emblem, belt, gauntlets, boots, and cape.
- Added glide controls, encounter HUD/objective updates, and boss encounter logic.
- Fixed duplicate `cape` declaration and Space’s accidental interaction trigger.
- Updated guard damage text from `5` to `3` and fixed singular/plural gear objective text.
- Verified the story can be advanced through all 12 chapters and the elevator transitions into Chapter 02 combat.

### Active
- Test combat balance and controls against regular enemies and Black Mask.
- Remove temporary `window.__gameTest` helper from `index.html`.
- Run `git diff --check` and a valid JavaScript syntax check.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Remove `window.__gameTest` from `index.html` after finishing its use for testing.
2. Use browser testing to check regular-enemy combat, guard, dodge, attacks, gliding, and Black Mask; review balance if needed.
3. Run `git diff --check` and a valid JavaScript syntax check.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game implementation; only modified file.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted.
- Cave gear and elevator progression were verified by calling `activateItem` through the temporary test hook; the test confirmed gear objectives update and `startCombat` begins Chapter 02 with three enemies and 100 health.
- Browser-input progression testing was inconsistent when advancing dialogue; the direct test hook was added temporarily and is still present.
- Earlier combat tests showed `BLOCKED — 3 DAMAGE`; rapid unguarded attacks resulted in defeat before eliminating enemies.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Improve the existing playable game while retaining its long story chapters; enhance the hero’s suit, add gliding, and introduce criminals and a villain encounter.

## Requirements
- Build on the existing game without asking clarifying questions.
- Keep the long chapters.

## Decisions
- Retained the existing story and added an East End crime encounter followed by a Black Mask-style boss fight.
- Added an armored suit, cape, and Space/on-screen glide controls.
- Slowed enemy attacks and reduced combat damage after testing showed the player was overwhelmed quickly.

## Work State
### Completed
- Updated the hero model with armor, cowl, emblem, belt, gauntlets, boots, and cape.
- Added glide controls, encounter HUD/objective updates, and boss encounter logic.
- Fixed duplicate `cape` declaration, Space’s accidental interaction trigger, guard damage text, and singular/plural gear objective text.
- Verified all 12 story chapters can advance and the elevator transitions into Chapter 02 combat.
- Removed the temporary `window.__gameTest` helper.
- `git diff --check` and JavaScript syntax check pass.

### Active
- Test combat balance and controls against regular enemies and Black Mask; prior combat tests were inconclusive because attacks did not reliably register.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Test regular-enemy combat, guard, dodge, attacks, gliding, and the Black Mask encounter in the browser.
2. Adjust combat balance or controls if testing reveals issues.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game implementation; only modified file.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted.
- Cave gear and elevator progression were verified using a temporary test hook; it confirmed gear objectives update and `startCombat` begins Chapter 02 with three enemies and 100 health. The helper has since been removed.
- Browser-input progression testing was inconsistent when advancing dialogue.
- Earlier combat tests showed `BLOCKED — 3 DAMAGE`; rapid unguarded attacks could defeat the player before eliminating enemies. Later testing still did not reliably register attacks.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Improve the existing playable game while retaining its long story chapters; enhance the hero’s suit, add gliding and utility tools, and introduce criminals and a villain encounter.

## Requirements
- Build on the existing game without asking clarifying questions.
- Keep the long story chapters.
- Make the night lighter, add grappling, batarang, and smoke-pellet controls, and separate criminals so they are encountered one at a time.

## Decisions
- Retained the story and added an East End crime encounter followed by a Black Mask-style boss fight.
- Added armored suit details, cape, and Space/on-screen glide controls.
- Slowed enemy attacks and reduced combat damage after testing showed the player was overwhelmed quickly.
- Began implementing brighter street lighting and one-at-a-time criminal encounters.

## Work State
### Completed
- Updated the hero model with armor, cowl, emblem, belt, gauntlets, boots, and cape.
- Added glide controls, encounter HUD/objective updates, and boss encounter logic.
- Fixed prior interaction, combat feedback, and objective-text issues.
- Verified all 12 story chapters can advance and the elevator transitions into Chapter 02 combat.
- Removed the temporary `window.__gameTest` helper.
- In `index.html`, lightened the vignette and East End scene, increased street-lamp lighting, updated combat utility text, added mobile buttons for batarang/grapple/smoke, and added initial utility-item state variables.

### Active
- Finish and test batarang, grapple, smoke-pellet mechanics and touch/keyboard bindings.
- Implement criminals activating one at a time.
- Test regular-enemy combat, guard, dodge, attacks, gliding, and the Black Mask encounter; earlier combat tests did not reliably register attacks.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Continue implementing the combat tools and sequential enemy activation in `index.html`.
2. Run syntax checks and test combat, lighting, and controls in the browser.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game implementation; only modified file.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted.
- Existing regular-enemy attacks use F and on-screen HIT; guard is R, dodge is Shift, and glide is Space.
- Current combat starts with three enemies; boss spawning occurs after all enemies are defeated.
- The latest edits declare utility state (`batarangs=3`, `smokePellets=2`, cooldowns, `smokeTimer`, `smokeCloud`) but do not yet implement their behavior.

## Objective
- Improve the existing playable game while preserving its long story chapters: enhance the hero’s suit, add gliding and utility tools, brighten the night, and stage criminals one at a time before a villain encounter.

## Requirements
- Build on the existing game without asking clarifying questions.
- Keep the long story chapters.
- Add grappling, batarang, and smoke-pellet controls; make the night lighter and criminals appear one at a time.

## Decisions
- Retained the story and added an East End crime encounter followed by a Black Mask-style boss fight.
- Added armored suit details, cape, and Space/on-screen glide controls.
- Slowed enemy attacks and reduced combat damage after testing showed the player was overwhelmed quickly.

## Work State
### Completed
- Updated the hero model with armor, cowl, emblem, belt, gauntlets, boots, and cape.
- Added glide controls, encounter HUD/objective updates, and boss encounter logic.
- Implemented brighter East End lighting and reduced the vignette.
- Added keyboard/touch controls and mechanics for batarang (Q), grapple (G), and smoke pellets (C).
- Implemented sequential criminal activation; only the active criminal approaches and attacks, with the boss appearing after the three criminals are defeated.
- Updated tool counts and combat tips; added smoke-screen visual and enemy stun effect.
- `git diff --check` passed.

### Active
- Validate JavaScript syntax and play-test the full game, especially utility tools, sequential enemies, combat controls, and the Black Mask encounter.
- Check mobile control layout and touch behavior after adding the extra combat buttons.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Run a syntax check on the module script in `index.html`.
2. Play-test the game through the cave and combat sequence; fix any issues found.
3. Review the final diff and report validation results.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game, story, scene, lighting, combat, and control implementation.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; `index.html` is the only modified file.
- The active enemy is selected via `activeEnemy()`; `hitEnemy()` advances the sequence or spawns the boss.
- Batarangs start at 3 and smoke pellets at 2; grapple has a cooldown and no ammunition count.

## Objective
- Improve the existing playable game while preserving its long story chapters: enhance the hero’s suit, add gliding and utility tools, brighten the night, and stage criminals one at a time before a villain encounter.

## Requirements
- Build on the existing game without asking clarifying questions.
- Keep the long story chapters.
- Add grappling, batarang, and smoke-pellet controls; brighten the night and make criminals appear one at a time.

## Decisions
- Retained the story and added an East End crime encounter followed by a Black Mask-style boss fight.
- Added armored suit details, cape, and Space/on-screen glide controls.
- Slowed enemy attacks and reduced combat damage after testing showed the player was overwhelmed quickly.

## Work State
### Completed
- Updated the hero model with armor, cowl, emblem, belt, gauntlets, boots, and cape.
- Added glide controls, encounter HUD/objective updates, and boss encounter logic.
- Brightened East End lighting and reduced the vignette.
- Added keyboard/touch controls for batarang (`Q`), grapple (`G`), and smoke pellets (`C`).
- Implemented sequential criminal activation; only the active criminal approaches and attacks, with the boss appearing after three criminals are defeated.
- Added tool counts, combat tips, smoke-screen visuals, and enemy stun effects.
- JavaScript module syntax check (`node --check /tmp/opencode/game-check.mjs`) and `git diff --check` passed.

### Active
- Play-test the game through the cave and combat sequence, including utility tools, Black Mask, and mobile touch layout.
- Review the final diff for issues.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Play-test the cave and combat sequence, including keyboard and touch controls.
2. Fix any issues found and rerun syntax and diff checks.
3. Review the final diff and report validation results.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game, story, scene, lighting, combat, and control implementation.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; `index.html` is the only modified file.
- `activeEnemy()` selects the current opponent; `hitEnemy()` advances the sequence or spawns the boss.
- Batarangs start at 3 and smoke pellets at 2; grapple has a cooldown and no ammunition count.

## Objective
- Improve the existing playable game while preserving its long story chapters: enhance the hero’s suit, add gliding and utility tools, brighten the night, and stage criminals one at a time before a villain encounter.

## Requirements
- Build on the existing game without asking clarifying questions.
- Keep the long story chapters.
- Add grappling, batarang, and smoke-pellet controls; brighten the night and make criminals appear one at a time.

## Decisions
- Retained the story and added an East End crime encounter followed by a Black Mask-style boss fight.
- Added armored suit details, a cape, and Space/on-screen glide controls.
- Slowed enemy attacks and reduced combat damage after testing showed the player was overwhelmed quickly.

## Work State
### Completed
- Updated the hero model with armor, cowl, emblem, belt, gauntlets, boots, and cape.
- Added glide controls, encounter HUD/objective updates, and boss encounter logic.
- Brightened East End lighting and reduced the vignette.
- Added keyboard/touch controls for batarang (`Q`), grapple (`G`), and smoke pellets (`C`).
- Implemented sequential criminal activation; the boss appears after three criminals are defeated.
- Added tool counts, combat tips, smoke-screen visuals, and enemy stun effects.
- Browser-tested the story opening, collected all cave gear, and entered combat.
- Verified batarang, grapple, smoke, guard, and glide inputs; confirmed defeating a criminal activates the next one.
- JavaScript module syntax check and `git diff --check` passed previously.

### Active
- Continue combat play-test through the third criminal and Black Mask encounter.
- Test mobile touch controls/layout.
- Review the final diff and rerun checks after any fixes.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Continue combat testing from the current state; verify the third criminal defeat triggers Black Mask and test the boss fight.
2. Check mobile touch layout and controls.
3. Review the final diff and rerun syntax and whitespace checks.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game story, scene, lighting, combat, and control implementation.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; `index.html` is the only modified file.
- Browser play-test collected all cave items and started combat.
- Three criminals are staged sequentially; the first two have been defeated and the third is active. The boss encounter is not yet tested.
- Batarangs start at 3 and smoke pellets at 2; grapple has a cooldown and no ammunition count.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Improve the existing playable game while preserving its long story chapters: enhance the hero’s suit, add gliding and utility tools, brighten the night, and stage criminals one at a time before a villain encounter.

## Requirements
- Build on the existing game without asking clarifying questions.
- Keep the long story chapters.
- Add grappling, batarang, and smoke-pellet controls; brighten the night and make criminals appear one at a time.

## Decisions
- Retained the story and added an East End crime encounter followed by a Black Mask-style boss fight.
- Added armored suit details, a cape, and Space/on-screen glide controls.
- Reduced incoming combat damage and made guarding fully block damage after play-testing showed the player was overwhelmed quickly.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Expand the existing Batman story game into roughly 40 chapters with cinematic scenes, collectible Riddler trophies, a visible grappling gun, and the requested villains.

## Requirements
- Preserve the existing game and story content while expanding it to about 40 chapters.
- Add a grappling gun, Riddler trophies, and scenes.
- Include Joker, Bane, Riddler, Two-Face, Killer Croc, Mad Hatter, and Mr. Freeze.

## Decisions
- Use villain-specific styling for story scene cards.
- The existing game already has a combat grapple control (`G`) and a grapple-gun cave pickup; the requested visible gun and broader progression still need implementation.

## Work State
### Completed
- Existing game improvements remain in place: armored Batman, glide, combat tools, brighter East End, sequential criminals, and Black Mask boss encounter.
- Added a trophy counter (`0 / 5`) to the HUD in `index.html`.
- Added a story scene-card element and villain-specific visual theme CSS in `index.html`.
- Reviewed the earlier browser console log: WebGL warnings and a missing favicon request were present, but no JavaScript errors; earlier syntax and diff checks passed.

### Active
- Expand the story from its current 11 beats to about 40 chapters, including the requested villains.
- Build out cinematic scenes and villain-specific story presentation.
- Implement actual Riddler trophy collectibles and collection behavior.
- Add a visible grappling gun to Batman and connect it to the existing grapple action.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect the current `index.html` edits and existing story progression before extending it.
2. Implement the 40-chapter structure, villain scenes, trophy placement/collection, and Batman’s grappling gun model.
3. Run syntax checks and browser-test chapter navigation, trophy collection, and grapple behavior.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Contains the game, current story beats, HUD, controls, combat, and recent partial scene/trophy UI edits.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; `index.html` is the only known modified repository file.
- The story currently contains 11 beats and labels its progress dynamically.
- A prior attempt to insert the grappling-gun model failed because the exact source snippet did not match; no model was added by that attempt.
- The new scene-card markup expects `storyScene`, `sceneTag`, and `sceneCaption`; scene rendering still needs to populate them.

{date:'GOTHAM · CASE FILE 01',title:'The question in the dark',villain:'riddler',scene:'THE NARROWS',caption:'A QUESTION WITH NO ANSWER',text:`

A green question mark is painted on the shutter of a closed pawnshop. Bruce photographs it from across the street. It is not a confession—just the first hint that someone wants the city to know he is watching.

Alfred finds a string of riddles in old police reports. Bruce files them away, unsure whether the author is a criminal, a prankster, or both.

`}, {date:'GOTHAM · CASE FILE 02',title:'A smile on the wire',villain:'joker',scene:'GOTHAM BROADCAST',caption:'LAUGHTER AFTER MIDNIGHT',text:`

Every screen in a downtown electronics shop flickers to life at once. A pale face smiles through the static, telling a joke no one in the room finds funny. The broadcast ends with a burst of confetti and a list of abandoned buildings.

Bruce watches the recording twice. The danger is not the punchline. It is how carefully the speaker studied his audience.

`}, {date:'GOTHAM · CASE FILE 03',title:'The coin that never lands',villain:'twoface',scene:'OLD COURTHOUSE',caption:'JUSTICE ON BOTH SIDES',text:`

Harvey Dent once believed a fair trial could change Gotham. Now a scarred former prosecutor lets a coin decide which version of justice will speak for him. One side is bright; the other is dark and worn.

Bruce keeps Harvey’s old campaign button beside the case notes. He will not reduce his friend to the damage done to him.

`}, {date:'GOTHAM · CASE FILE 04',title:'Something beneath the river',villain:'croc',scene:'EAST END DRAINS',caption:'EYES BELOW THE WATER',text:`

Workers refuse to enter a storm tunnel after hearing heavy footsteps beneath the grates. A hulking figure is seen only in the ripples and the brief flash of yellow eyes.

The newspapers call him a monster. Bruce writes a different question in the margin: what happened to the boy before the city gave him that name?

`}, {date:'GOTHAM · CASE FILE 05',title:'The tea-party invitation',villain:'hatter',scene:'ABANDONED THEATER',caption:'ONE SEAT LEFT EMPTY',text:`

In a derelict playhouse, a tiny paper invitation waits on a velvet chair. It promises a perfect world to anyone willing to follow the White Rabbit. The ink is fresh; the theater has been empty for years.

Bruce recognizes the language of a trap dressed as comfort. Some people do not want power over a city. They want power over one person at a time.

`}, {date:'GOTHAM · CASE FILE 06',title:'The cold front',villain:'freeze',scene:'GOTHAM HARBOR',caption:'WINTER IN THE WRONG SEASON',text:`

A shipment of medical equipment disappears from a waterfront laboratory. Frost feathers the inside of a locked storage door, though the night outside is warm.

The lead points to Victor Fries, a scientist trying to keep his wife alive. Bruce marks the name carefully. A desperate motive does not make dangerous methods harmless.

`}, {date:'GOTHAM · CASE FILE 07',title:'The man who broke a wall',villain:'bane',scene:'BLACKGATE PRISON',caption:'STRENGTH IS A STRATEGY',text:`

A transfer report describes a prisoner who studies every guard rotation and every weakness in the building. Bane does not waste strength; he saves it for the moment it matters.

Bruce adds endurance drills to his training. Winning a fight, he realizes, may begin long before the first blow.

`}, {date:'GOTHAM · CASE FILE 08',title:'The clown’s calling card',villain:'joker',scene:'MONTOYA CIRCUS',caption:'THE SHOW WILL GO ON',text:`

A shuttered circus tent is found ringed with playing cards. Somewhere inside, a music box turns by itself. The officers who enter hear applause from an empty grandstand.

Bruce studies the scene photographs. The performer wants fear, but he also wants an audience. That need may be the most dangerous clue of all.

`}, {date:'GOTHAM · CASE FILE 09',title:'A city-sized puzzle',villain:'riddler',scene:'FINANCIAL DISTRICT',caption:'FOLLOW THE GREEN LIGHT',text:`

Traffic signals across three blocks change in a sequence that spells out a riddle. The pattern leads to a locked service room—and a second riddle hidden inside it.

Bruce maps the route without entering the buildings. Whoever designed the game is testing patience as much as intelligence.

`}, {date:'GOTHAM · CASE FILE 10',title:'Harvey’s other face',villain:'twoface',scene:'GOTHAM CENTRAL',caption:'A COIN IN THE EVIDENCE ROOM',text:`

A witness refuses to testify after receiving a silver coin with a scorched edge. Harvey’s old colleagues want to protect him from the investigation; Harvey would have demanded the truth.

Bruce asks Alfred to keep the original case files safe. Memory can preserve a person’s best self, even when the present tries to erase it.

`}, {date:'GOTHAM · CASE FILE 11',title:'The king below',villain:'croc',scene:'OLD SEWER LINE',caption:'THE TUNNELS HAVE A KING',text:`

A missing-persons report leads to a forgotten passage beneath the river. The marks on the concrete are too high for an ordinary man, and the torn steel bars bend outward.

Bruce brings a rescue map to the police instead of charging underground alone. Preparation is not cowardice; it is how you make sure someone comes back.

`}, {date:'GOTHAM · CASE FILE 12',title:'A dream with locked doors',villain:'hatter',scene:'WONDERLAND ROOM',caption:'WAKE UP, GOTHAM',text:`

Several people describe the same impossible tea party, down to the ticking clock and the empty chair. Their accounts point toward a doctor who has learned to make fantasy feel safer than waking life.

Bruce begins reading about coercion and trauma. The mind is not a puzzle box to force open. A victim needs a way out, not another person holding the key.

`}, {date:'GOTHAM · CASE FILE 13',title:'A promise in the ice',villain:'freeze',scene:'CRYOGENICS LAB',caption:'LOVE FROZEN IN TIME',text:`

Victor Fries leaves a message asking for a single component to stabilize Nora’s chamber. It is the first time his trail sounds less like a threat and more like a plea.

Bruce asks Wayne Medical to review the research. There may be a way to help without letting a desperate man endanger anyone else.

`}, {date:'GOTHAM · CASE FILE 14',title:'Bane’s careful silence',villain:'bane',scene:'PORT ADAMS',caption:'THE STRONGEST MAN WAITS',text:`

A crate of experimental medical supplies vanishes from the port. The theft is clean, with no broken locks and no witnesses willing to talk. Bane has made the city look in the wrong direction.

Bruce studies the timing. A patient opponent can turn a city’s routines into a weapon.

`}, {date:'GOTHAM · CASE FILE 15',title:'The punchline is a warning',villain:'joker',scene:'PARK ROW',caption:'NO ONE IS LAUGHING',text:`

At a charity hall, the lights go out for eleven seconds. When they return, every guest has a paper smile on the table and the donation ledger is gone. No one is hurt, but the message is unmistakable.

Bruce asks the staff what they saw before asking what they lost. Fear makes people forget that their safety matters more than a ledger.

`}, {date:'GOTHAM · CASE FILE 16',title:'Riddles on the rooftops',villain:'riddler',scene:'ROOFTOP GRID',caption:'THE NEXT CLUE IS ABOVE YOU',text:`

Green markers appear on rooftops overlooking the financial district. Each one points to a place where Gotham failed someone: a shuttered clinic, an empty school, a neglected shelter.

Bruce sees the cruelty inside the cleverness. The Riddler may know the city’s wounds, but he treats them as props in a game.

`}, {date:'GOTHAM · CASE FILE 17',title:'The courthouse divided',villain:'twoface',scene:'GOTHAM COURTHOUSE',caption:'ONE VERDICT, TWO OUTCOMES',text:`

Harvey sends a sealed envelope to Bruce. Inside is a list of people he wants protected from his own gang. The handwriting shifts from careful to jagged halfway down the page.

Bruce does not mistake the letter for an apology. He sees it as a chance to keep innocent people out of the crossfire.

`}, {date:'GOTHAM · CASE FILE 18',title:'The river remembers',villain:'croc',scene:'FLOODED UNDERPASS',caption:'A RESCUE IN THE DARK',text:`

Rising water traps a maintenance crew in a tunnel. Something moves beneath the surface, then lifts a steel gate from its hinges. The workers emerge shaken but alive.

Bruce cannot tell whether Croc saved them or simply cleared his path. Either way, the next search will need a boat, a plan, and a team.

`}, {date:'GOTHAM · CASE FILE 19',title:'The clockwork rabbit',villain:'hatter',scene:'CLOCKTOWER',caption:'TIME IS RUNNING OUT',text:`

A clocktower chimes thirteen times. A trail of brass gears leads to a locked room where a frightened witness has been hidden in plain sight.

Alfred reminds Bruce that rescuing someone means listening to them after the danger passes. The exit is only the beginning of feeling safe again.

`}, {date:'GOTHAM · CASE FILE 20',title:'Whiteout at the docks',villain:'freeze',scene:'GOTHAM DOCKS',caption:'THE HARBOR TURNS TO GLASS',text:`

A wave of freezing mist crawls across the docks as Victor tries to retrieve a power cell. Workers are stranded behind the ice, too afraid to cross the slick metal walkways.

Bruce coordinates a safe evacuation with the harbor crew. He will face Fries if he must, but the people in danger come first.

`}, {date:'GOTHAM · CASE FILE 21',title:'A test of endurance',villain:'bane',scene:'NARROWS ROOFLINE',caption:'NO SHORTCUT THROUGH FEAR',text:`

Bane leaves a trail of staged emergencies across the Narrows. Each one forces responders to split their attention. The trap is not a single fight; it is exhaustion.

Bruce changes the plan: call in help, rotate teams, and refuse to let pride set the pace. The city is stronger when no one has to carry it alone.

`}, {date:'GOTHAM · CASE FILE 22',title:'The joker takes the stage',villain:'joker',scene:'MONTOYA PLAYHOUSE',caption:'THE HOUSE LIGHTS GO OUT',text:`

The old playhouse is filled with laughing recordings and painted spotlights. The Joker wants the entire city to watch his performance, but the people inside are not an audience—they are hostages.

Bruce studies the exits first. A dramatic entrance can wait until everyone has a way out.

`}, {date:'GOTHAM · CASE FILE 23',title:'The answer beneath the question',villain:'riddler',scene:'WAYNE STATION',caption:'EVERY CLUE LEAVES A TRACE',text:`

A final riddle points to a substation carrying power to a hospital. Bruce spots the hidden override before the lights go out and alerts the engineers.

The puzzle is solved, but the lesson is larger: cleverness without care can become another kind of cruelty.

`}, {date:'GOTHAM · CASE FILE 24',title:'A chance for Harvey',villain:'twoface',scene:'ACE CHEMICALS',caption:'THE COIN FALLS',text:`

Harvey’s crew corners a bookkeeper who once helped build his career. The coin spins across a catwalk and lands on the scarred side. Bruce steps between them before the verdict can become irreversible.

He speaks to Harvey by name, not by nickname. One honest voice cannot undo everything, but it can leave a door open.

`}, {date:'GOTHAM · CASE FILE 25',title:'A truce in the tunnels',villain:'croc',scene:'UNDERCITY',caption:'THE WAY OUT IS TOGETHER',text:`

Bruce finds Croc guarding a group of unhoused people from a collapsing tunnel. Neither trusts the other, but the roof is coming down and there is no time for an argument.

They guide everyone to the surface. Croc disappears before the police arrive, leaving Bruce with more questions than answers—and one less reason to call him a monster.

`}, {date:'GOTHAM · CASE FILE 26',title:'The last tea party',villain:'hatter',scene:'WINTER GARDEN',caption:'THE CLOCK STOPS HERE',text:`

The Mad Hatter’s elaborate set is built around a greenhouse clock. The people he drew into his fantasy are scared, confused, and ready to choose their own way home.

Bruce keeps his voice calm and the room bright. The spell ends not with a punch, but with each guest remembering their own name.

`}, {date:'GOTHAM · CASE FILE 27',title:'A cure is not a cure',villain:'freeze',scene:'GOTHAM MEDICAL',caption:'HOPE NEEDS MORE THAN ICE',text:`

Victor’s power cell is recovered before the laboratory fails. The research is imperfect, but the doctors find a safer path to keep Nora stable while they continue their work.

Fries surrenders without a fight. Bruce sees a future case that may not need to be a battle at all.

`}, {date:'GOTHAM · CASE FILE 28',title:'The city wakes',villain:'bane',scene:'GOTHAM ROOFTOPS',caption:'DAWN OVER THE NARROWS',text:`

Bane’s final move is a coordinated strike meant to make Gotham believe resistance is pointless. Instead, neighbors open doors, medics share supplies, and officers protect the evacuation routes.

Bruce faces Bane after the last civilians are safe. Strength matters, but it is not the only strength in the city.

`}, {date:'GOTHAM · BEFORE DAWN',title:'A place to begin',scene:'WAYNE CAVE',caption:'ONE PROMISE. ONE FIRST STEP.',text:'

Alfred has left the gear ready: the field guide on the bench, prototypes on the armor table, the suit in its display frame, and the Batmobile resting beneath the stone ceiling. The elevator waits at the far end of the cave. Nothing here is finished, and nobody pretends otherwise.

Bruce takes in the quiet workshop and the steady lights. Beyond the cave lies a city full of strangers, each with a story he cannot know yet. He cannot undo the night that changed his life. He can choose what he does with the nights still ahead.

One man. One promise. A first step into the dark.

Explore the cave, inspect every piece of equipment, collect Riddler trophies, and take the elevator when you are ready.

'}

Index: index.html =================================================================== --- index.html +++ index.html @@ -149,9 +149,37 @@ {date:'WAYNE CAVE · A RETURN',title:'An unexpected ally',text:'

“Excuse me, sir. Remember me?” The man sets down the thermos. “I’m Alfred.” Bruce has known him all his life, of course, but down here they meet differently: not as employer and servant, nor as grieving boy and patient guardian, but as two people looking at the same unfinished room.

Alfred has sketched a workbench, a computer station, and a safer route back to the house. He has also found a book on self-defense. Bruce studies the pages and recognizes how much he does not know. Alfred does not gloat. He pours tea.

“You’ll need more than determination, sir,” he says. “Determination is what gets you to the door. Preparation is what gets you home.”

'}, {date:'WAYNE CAVE · THE PLAN TAKES SHAPE',title:'Tools, not answers',text:'

They work in fits and starts. Alfred knows how to keep a project moving; Bruce knows how to ask questions that make the project bigger. The computer station becomes a place to sort reports and maps. A suit bay takes shape against the stone. The elevator connects the cave to the estate without sending either man through the front hall.

Every object has a purpose and a limit. Batarangs can distract or disarm, but they cannot make a bad decision wise. Smoke pellets can cover a retreat, but they cannot turn a retreat into a victory. A grapple prototype can bridge a gap only if the person using it thinks before leaping.

Bruce begins to see the cave not as a lair, but as a workshop for learning how to help.

'}, {date:'WAYNE CAVE · THE VEHICLE BAY',title:'A machine with sharp edges',text:'

The car is the most ambitious piece of the plan and the least finished. Its armored panels catch the work lights; its engine answers a test with a growl that makes dust fall from the ceiling. Alfred circles it with a clipboard, noting what still needs attention.

“It’s not quite street legal,” he says. “And I would avoid the red switch.” Bruce asks if it is safe. Alfred considers the question for a beat too long. They agree to call it a prototype and to keep the first test somewhere far from traffic.

The machine represents possibility, but also temptation: the urge to make an entrance instead of doing the patient work. Bruce closes the hood. Tonight, the car can wait.

'}, {date:'WAYNE CAVE · BEFORE DAWN',title:'The first lesson',text:'

Alfred lays the self-defense field guide on the workbench. It is not as impressive as the suit, the car, or the glowing computer screens. Its pages are worn at the corners, full of diagrams and notes in Alfred’s neat hand. Bruce opens it carefully.

“Begin with the book,” Alfred tells him. “Learn how to keep your balance. Learn when to move, when to listen, and when walking away is the bravest thing you can do.” Bruce looks toward the equipment waiting around the cave. For the first time, it feels less like a collection of answers and more like a list of responsibilities.

There is still a long way to go. But the work has finally begun.

`}, +{date:'GOTHAM · CASE FILE 27',title:'A cure is not a cure',villain:'freeze',scene:'GOTHAM MEDICAL',caption:'HOPE NEEDS MORE THAN ICE',text:`

Victor’s power cell is recovered before the laboratory fails. The research is imperfect, but the doctors find a safer path to keep Nora stable while they continue their work.

Fries surrenders without a fight. Bruce sees a future case that may not need to be a battle at all.

`}, +{date:'GOTHAM · CASE FILE 28',title:'The city wakes',villain:'bane',scene:'GOTHAM ROOFTOPS',caption:'DAWN OVER THE NARROWS',text:`

Bane’s final move is a coordinated strike meant to make Gotham believe resistance is pointless. Instead, neighbors open doors, medics share supplies, and officers protect the evacuation routes.

Bruce faces Bane after the last civilians are safe. Strength matters, but it is not the only strength in the city.

`}, +{date:'GOTHAM · BEFORE DAWN',title:'A place to begin',scene:'WAYNE CAVE',caption:'ONE PROMISE. ONE FIRST STEP.',text:'

Alfred has left the gear ready: the field guide on the bench, prototypes on the armor table, the suit in its display frame, and the Batmobile resting beneath the stone ceiling. The elevator waits at the far end of the cave. Nothing here is finished, and nobody pretends otherwise.

Bruce takes in the quiet workshop and the steady lights. Beyond the cave lies a city full of strangers, each with a story he cannot know yet. He cannot undo the night that changed his life. He can choose what he does with the nights still ahead.

One man. One promise. A first step into the dark.

Explore the cave, inspect every piece of equipment, collect Riddler trophies, and take the elevator when you are ready.

## Objective
- Expand the existing Batman story game to about 40 chapters with cinematic scenes, Riddler trophies, a visible grappling gun, and the requested villains.

## Requirements
- Preserve the existing game and story content while expanding it to about 40 chapters.
- Add a grappling gun, Riddler trophy collectibles, and scenes.
- Include Joker, Bane, Riddler, Two-Face, Killer Croc, Mad Hatter, and Mr. Freeze.

## Decisions
- Use villain-specific styling for story scene cards.
- Keep trophy collection optional so it does not block cave progression.
- Reveal the grappling gun model when Bruce collects the grapple gun pickup.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added five Riddler trophy pickups in the cave, with glowing question-mark models and a HUD counter.
- Added a holstered grappling-gun model to Batman; collecting the cave pickup reveals it.
- Replaced the final story beat with expanded Gotham case-file chapters involving the requested villains; the intended total is 40 beats.

### Active
- Wire story beat scene metadata (`villain`, `scene`, `caption`) into the scene card; `renderBeat()` currently only updates date, title, and story text.
- Verify the story has exactly 40 entries and that chapter progress, scenes, collectibles, and grapple behavior work correctly.
- Run syntax checks and browser-test the game.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Update `renderBeat()` to populate `storyScene`’s villain styling, `sceneTag`, and `sceneCaption`.
2. Verify the story beat count is exactly 40 and check chapter/progress presentation.
3. Run syntax checks and browser-test trophy pickup/counting, grapple pickup/visibility, and progression.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game, story beats, scene card markup/styles, collectibles, Batman model, and grapple behavior.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; `index.html` is the only known modified file.
- The grapple action is combat-only and uses `G`; its gameplay function predates the new visible model.
- Scene-card markup already includes `storyScene`, `sceneTag`, and `sceneCaption`, but rendering has not yet been connected to beat metadata.

Gotham’s old theater empties into a rain-bright street. Thomas and Martha Wayne walk home with their young son, Bruce, still talking about the film. His mother holds his hand; his father listens as if the story matters as much as the night is beautiful.

Their shortcut passes a narrow alley. A stranger steps from the dark and asks for money. Thomas does not reach for a weapon or shout. He gives the gunman $200—everything he has—and tries to make himself the only danger in the alley.

“Take it. Just let my family go.”

For one suspended second, the city seems to hold its breath.

'}, 143: {date:'GOTHAM CITY · THAT NIGHT',title:'The promise',text:'

The gunshot cracks across the street. Thomas and Martha fall beneath the streetlamp. Bruce is left kneeling beside them, surrounded by a city that keeps moving but will never look the same to him again.

In the weeks that follow, adults speak softly around him. They tell him he is safe now, that the police will find the killer, that time will make the pain smaller. None of those words can bring his parents back. Bruce learns that helplessness can feel louder than any siren.

Grief hardens into a promise—not a plan yet, only a vow he will carry into every room: no one else should have to feel this alone.

'}, 144: {date:'WAYNE MANOR · THE YEARS AFTER',title:'A house full of echoes',text:'

The manor is enormous, but after the funeral it feels too quiet. Bruce grows up among portraits, locked rooms, and the careful kindness of the family’s longtime butler, Alfred Pennyworth. Alfred makes breakfast, remembers birthdays, and never asks Bruce to pretend he is all right.

Bruce studies, travels, and searches for a way to understand the violence that took his parents. He learns how fear works, how people survive, and how easily a powerful family can mistake its own comfort for the health of its city.

The promise stays with him. It changes shape as he does: first a child’s wish, then a question, and finally a responsibility he cannot hand to anyone else.

'}, 145: {date:'GOTHAM CITY · 2008',title:'A fortune, a house, a name',text:'

Twenty-six years later, Bruce uncovers a fortune his father had quietly set aside—seed money for a plan Thomas never finished. Bruce invests it, buys back a neglected mansion, and gives the work a public name: Wayne Enterprises.

From the outside, it looks like a return to the life he was born to lead. The grand rooms fill with donors, champagne, and polished promises. Harvey Dent, Gotham’s tireless district attorney, is among the guests. He believes the city can be repaired through courage and honest institutions.

Bruce admires that conviction. He also knows how many people are waiting for someone else to fix things. Behind the parties, he begins asking harder questions about what a single person can do.

'}, 146: {date:'GOTHAM CITY · 2009',title:'The cost of hope',text:'

A year later, a terrible incident leaves Harvey Dent’s face scarred and his life changed. The city’s bright public hope is suddenly vulnerable to pain, anger, and the cruel appetite of headlines. Bruce watches the damage from a distance and recognizes the same old feeling: the moment when safety proves it was never guaranteed.

He retreats from the parties and the easy explanations. With a bag in hand, he descends beneath Wayne Manor into a forgotten cave. The stone is cold, the passages are rough, and the darkness seems almost honest. Here, at least, nobody asks him to smile for a photograph.

For a while, Bruce tells himself solitude is the same thing as purpose.

'}, 147: {date:'WAYNE CAVE · THE FIRST VISIT',title:'A man in the dark',text:'

“Excuse me, sir. Are you looking for something?” an old man calls from the cave entrance. “There’s nothing in here. It’s old—just like me.”

Bruce bristles. “I’m trying to do something with this place. What makes you think you can tell me what to do?” The stranger does not rise to the challenge. He simply points out that Bruce is standing on private property and waits for him to answer.

Bruce refuses to leave. The old man gives him one last look and walks away. The exchange is awkward, almost absurd, but it stays with Bruce. Someone has finally spoken to him plainly, without fear of his name or his money.

'}, 148: {date:'WAYNE CAVE · THREE MONTHS LATER',title:'The long quiet',text:'

Days pass. Bruce returns to the cave with tools, then with plans, then with nothing but questions. He measures the cavern and marks out possible work areas. He tries to turn the rock into a headquarters by force of will, but every task exposes another one he does not know how to do.

Above him, the manor continues its routines. Below, the cave answers with drips of water and the occasional flutter of wings. Bruce begins to understand that a mission built alone may only become another way to hide.

One evening he hears footsteps at the entrance. The same old man has come back. This time, he is carrying a thermos and a small stack of notes.

'}, 149: {date:'WAYNE CAVE · A RETURN',title:'An unexpected ally',text:'

“Excuse me, sir. Remember me?” The man sets down the thermos. “I’m Alfred.” Bruce has known him all his life, of course, but down here they meet differently: not as employer and servant, nor as grieving boy and patient guardian, but as two people looking at the same unfinished room.

Alfred has sketched a workbench, a computer station, and a safer route back to the house. He has also found a book on self-defense. Bruce studies the pages and recognizes how much he does not know. Alfred does not gloat. He pours tea.

“You’ll need more than determination, sir,” he says. “Determination is what gets you to the door. Preparation is what gets you home.”

'}, 150: {date:'WAYNE CAVE · THE PLAN TAKES SHAPE',title:'Tools, not answers',text:'

They work in fits and starts. Alfred knows how to keep a project moving; Bruce knows how to ask questions that make the project bigger. The computer station becomes a place to sort reports and maps. A suit bay takes shape against the stone. The elevator connects the cave to the estate without sending either man through the front hall.

Every object has a purpose and a limit. Batarangs can distract or disarm, but they cannot make a bad decision wise. Smoke pellets can cover a retreat, but they cannot turn a retreat into a victory. A grapple prototype can bridge a gap only if the person using it thinks before leaping.

Bruce begins to see the cave not as a lair, but as a workshop for learning how to help.

'}, 151: {date:'WAYNE CAVE · THE VEHICLE BAY',title:'A machine with sharp edges',text:'

The car is the most ambitious piece of the plan and the least finished. Its armored panels catch the work lights; its engine answers a test with a growl that makes dust fall from the ceiling. Alfred circles it with a clipboard, noting what still needs attention.

“It’s not quite street legal,” he says. “And I would avoid the red switch.” Bruce asks if it is safe. Alfred considers the question for a beat too long. They agree to call it a prototype and to keep the first test somewhere far from traffic.

The machine represents possibility, but also temptation: the urge to make an entrance instead of doing the patient work. Bruce closes the hood. Tonight, the car can wait.

'}, 152: {date:'WAYNE CAVE · BEFORE DAWN',title:'The first lesson',text:'

Alfred lays the self-defense field guide on the workbench. It is not as impressive as the suit, the car, or the glowing computer screens. Its pages are worn at the corners, full of diagrams and notes in Alfred’s neat hand. Bruce opens it carefully.

“Begin with the book,” Alfred tells him. “Learn how to keep your balance. Learn when to move, when to listen, and when walking away is the bravest thing you can do.” Bruce looks toward the equipment waiting around the cave. For the first time, it feels less like a collection of answers and more like a list of responsibilities.

There is still a long way to go. But the work has finally begun.

'}, 153: {date:'GOTHAM · CASE FILE 01',title:'The question in the dark',villain:'riddler',scene:'THE NARROWS',caption:'A QUESTION WITH NO ANSWER',text:`

A green question mark is painted on the shutter of a closed pawnshop. Bruce photographs it from across the street. It is not a confession—just the first hint that someone wants the city to know he is watching.

Alfred finds a string of riddles in old police reports. Bruce files them away, unsure whether the author is a criminal, a prankster, or both.

`}, 154: {date:'GOTHAM · CASE FILE 02',title:'A smile on the wire',villain:'joker',scene:'GOTHAM BROADCAST',caption:'LAUGHTER AFTER MIDNIGHT',text:`

Every screen in a downtown electronics shop flickers to life at once. A pale face smiles through the static, telling a joke no one in the room finds funny. The broadcast ends with a burst of confetti and a list of abandoned buildings.

Bruce watches the recording twice. The danger is not the punchline. It is how carefully the speaker studied his audience.

`}, 155: {date:'GOTHAM · CASE FILE 03',title:'The coin that never lands',villain:'twoface',scene:'OLD COURTHOUSE',caption:'JUSTICE ON BOTH SIDES',text:`

Harvey Dent once believed a fair trial could change Gotham. Now a scarred former prosecutor lets a coin decide which version of justice will speak for him. One side is bright; the other is dark and worn.

Bruce keeps Harvey’s old campaign button beside the case notes. He will not reduce his friend to the damage done to him.

`}, 156: {date:'GOTHAM · CASE FILE 04',title:'Something beneath the river',villain:'croc',scene:'EAST END DRAINS',caption:'EYES BELOW THE WATER',text:`

Workers refuse to enter a storm tunnel after hearing heavy footsteps beneath the grates. A hulking figure is seen only in the ripples and the brief flash of yellow eyes.

The newspapers call him a monster. Bruce writes a different question in the margin: what happened to the boy before the city gave him that name?

`}, 157: {date:'GOTHAM · CASE FILE 05',title:'The tea-party invitation',villain:'hatter',scene:'ABANDONED THEATER',caption:'ONE SEAT LEFT EMPTY',text:`

In a derelict playhouse, a tiny paper invitation waits on a velvet chair. It promises a perfect world to anyone willing to follow the White Rabbit. The ink is fresh; the theater has been empty for years.

Bruce recognizes the language of a trap dressed as comfort. Some people do not want power over a city. They want power over one person at a time.

`}, 158: {date:'GOTHAM · CASE FILE 06',title:'The cold front',villain:'freeze',scene:'GOTHAM HARBOR',caption:'WINTER IN THE WRONG SEASON',text:`

A shipment of medical equipment disappears from a waterfront laboratory. Frost feathers the inside of a locked storage door, though the night outside is warm.

The lead points to Victor Fries, a scientist trying to keep his wife alive. Bruce marks the name carefully. A desperate motive does not make dangerous methods harmless.

`}, 159: {date:'GOTHAM · CASE FILE 07',title:'The man who broke a wall',villain:'bane',scene:'BLACKGATE PRISON',caption:'STRENGTH IS A STRATEGY',text:`

A transfer report describes a prisoner who studies every guard rotation and every weakness in the building. Bane does not waste strength; he saves it for the moment it matters.

Bruce adds endurance drills to his training. Winning a fight, he realizes, may begin long before the first blow.

`}, 160: {date:'GOTHAM · CASE FILE 08',title:'The clown’s calling card',villain:'joker',scene:'MONTOYA CIRCUS',caption:'THE SHOW WILL GO ON',text:`

A shuttered circus tent is found ringed with playing cards. Somewhere inside, a music box turns by itself. The officers who enter hear applause from an empty grandstand.

Bruce studies the scene photographs. The performer wants fear, but he also wants an audience. That need may be the most dangerous clue of all.

`}, 161: {date:'GOTHAM · CASE FILE 09',title:'A city-sized puzzle',villain:'riddler',scene:'FINANCIAL DISTRICT',caption:'FOLLOW THE GREEN LIGHT',text:`

Traffic signals across three blocks change in a sequence that spells out a riddle. The pattern leads to a locked service room—and a second riddle hidden inside it.

Bruce maps the route without entering the buildings. Whoever designed the game is testing patience as much as intelligence.

`}, 162: {date:'GOTHAM · CASE FILE 10',title:'Harvey’s other face',villain:'twoface',scene:'GOTHAM CENTRAL',caption:'A COIN IN THE EVIDENCE ROOM',text:`

A witness refuses to testify after receiving a silver coin with a scorched edge. Harvey’s old colleagues want to protect him from the investigation; Harvey would have demanded the truth.

Bruce asks Alfred to keep the original case files safe. Memory can preserve a person’s best self, even when the present tries to erase it.

`}, 163: {date:'GOTHAM · CASE FILE 11',title:'The king below',villain:'croc',scene:'OLD SEWER LINE',caption:'THE TUNNELS HAVE A KING',text:`

A missing-persons report leads to a forgotten passage beneath the river. The marks on the concrete are too high for an ordinary man, and the torn steel bars bend outward.

Bruce brings a rescue map to the police instead of charging underground alone. Preparation is not cowardice; it is how you make sure someone comes back.

`}, 164: {date:'GOTHAM · CASE FILE 12',title:'A dream with locked doors',villain:'hatter',scene:'WONDERLAND ROOM',caption:'WAKE UP, GOTHAM',text:`

Several people describe the same impossible tea party, down to the ticking clock and the empty chair. Their accounts point toward a doctor who has learned to make fantasy feel safer than waking life.

Bruce begins reading about coercion and trauma. The mind is not a puzzle box to force open. A victim needs a way out, not another person holding the key.

`}, 165: {date:'GOTHAM · CASE FILE 13',title:'A promise in the ice',villain:'freeze',scene:'CRYOGENICS LAB',caption:'LOVE FROZEN IN TIME',text:`

Victor Fries leaves a message asking for a single component to stabilize Nora’s chamber. It is the first time his trail sounds less like a threat and more like a plea.

Bruce asks Wayne Medical to review the research. There may be a way to help without letting a desperate man endanger anyone else.

`}, 166: {date:'GOTHAM · CASE FILE 14',title:'Bane’s careful silence',villain:'bane',scene:'PORT ADAMS',caption:'THE STRONGEST MAN WAITS',text:`

A crate of experimental medical supplies vanishes from the port. The theft is clean, with no broken locks and no witnesses willing to talk. Bane has made the city look in the wrong direction.

Bruce studies the timing. A patient opponent can turn a city’s routines into a weapon.

`}, 167: {date:'GOTHAM · CASE FILE 15',title:'The punchline is a warning',villain:'joker',scene:'PARK ROW',caption:'NO ONE IS LAUGHING',text:`

At a charity hall, the lights go out for eleven seconds. When they return, every guest has a paper smile on the table and the donation ledger is gone. No one is hurt, but the message is unmistakable.

Bruce asks the staff what they saw before asking what they lost. Fear makes people forget that their safety matters more than a ledger.

`}, 168: {date:'GOTHAM · CASE FILE 16',title:'Riddles on the rooftops',villain:'riddler',scene:'ROOFTOP GRID',caption:'THE NEXT CLUE IS ABOVE YOU',text:`

Green markers appear on rooftops overlooking the financial district. Each one points to a place where Gotham failed someone: a shuttered clinic, an empty school, a neglected shelter.

Bruce sees the cruelty inside the cleverness. The Riddler may know the city’s wounds, but he treats them as props in a game.

`}, 169: {date:'GOTHAM · CASE FILE 17',title:'The courthouse divided',villain:'twoface',scene:'GOTHAM COURTHOUSE',caption:'ONE VERDICT, TWO OUTCOMES',text:`

Harvey sends a sealed envelope to Bruce. Inside is a list of people he wants protected from his own gang. The handwriting shifts from careful to jagged halfway down the page.

Bruce does not mistake the letter for an apology. He sees it as a chance to keep innocent people out of the crossfire.

`}, 170: {date:'GOTHAM · CASE FILE 18',title:'The river remembers',villain:'croc',scene:'FLOODED UNDERPASS',caption:'A RESCUE IN THE DARK',text:`

Rising water traps a maintenance crew in a tunnel. Something moves beneath the surface, then lifts a steel gate from its hinges. The workers emerge shaken but alive.

Bruce cannot tell whether Croc saved them or simply cleared his path. Either way, the next search will need a boat, a plan, and a team.

`}, 171: {date:'GOTHAM · CASE FILE 19',title:'The clockwork rabbit',villain:'hatter',scene:'CLOCKTOWER',caption:'TIME IS RUNNING OUT',text:`

A clocktower chimes thirteen times. A trail of brass gears leads to a locked room where a frightened witness has been hidden in plain sight.

Alfred reminds Bruce that rescuing someone means listening to them after the danger passes. The exit is only the beginning of feeling safe again.

`}, 172: {date:'GOTHAM · CASE FILE 20',title:'Whiteout at the docks',villain:'freeze',scene:'GOTHAM DOCKS',caption:'THE HARBOR TURNS TO GLASS',text:`

A wave of freezing mist crawls across the docks as Victor tries to retrieve a power cell. Workers are stranded behind the ice, too afraid to cross the slick metal walkways.

Bruce coordinates a safe evacuation with the harbor crew. He will face Fries if he must, but the people in danger come first.

`}, 173: {date:'GOTHAM · CASE FILE 21',title:'A test of endurance',villain:'bane',scene:'NARROWS ROOFLINE',caption:'NO SHORTCUT THROUGH FEAR',text:`

Bane leaves a trail of staged emergencies across the Narrows. Each one forces responders to split their attention. The trap is not a single fight; it is exhaustion.

Bruce changes the plan: call in help, rotate teams, and refuse to let pride set the pace. The city is stronger when no one has to carry it alone.

`}, 174: {date:'GOTHAM · CASE FILE 22',title:'The joker takes the stage',villain:'joker',scene:'MONTOYA PLAYHOUSE',caption:'THE HOUSE LIGHTS GO OUT',text:`

The old playhouse is filled with laughing recordings and painted spotlights. The Joker wants the entire city to watch his performance, but the people inside are not an audience—they are hostages.

Bruce studies the exits first. A dramatic entrance can wait until everyone has a way out.

`}, 175: {date:'GOTHAM · CASE FILE 23',title:'The answer beneath the question',villain:'riddler',scene:'WAYNE STATION',caption:'EVERY CLUE LEAVES A TRACE',text:`

A final riddle points to a substation carrying power to a hospital. Bruce spots the hidden override before the lights go out and alerts the engineers.

The puzzle is solved, but the lesson is larger: cleverness without care can become another kind of cruelty.

`}, 176: {date:'GOTHAM · CASE FILE 24',title:'A chance for Harvey',villain:'twoface',scene:'ACE CHEMICALS',caption:'THE COIN FALLS',text:`

Harvey’s crew corners a bookkeeper who once helped build his career. The coin spins across a catwalk and lands on the scarred side. Bruce steps between them before the verdict can become irreversible.

He speaks to Harvey by name, not by nickname. One honest voice cannot undo everything, but it can leave a door open.

`}, 177: {date:'GOTHAM · CASE FILE 25',title:'A truce in the tunnels',villain:'croc',scene:'UNDERCITY',caption:'THE WAY OUT IS TOGETHER',text:`

Bruce finds Croc guarding a group of unhoused people from a collapsing tunnel. Neither trusts the other, but the roof is coming down and there is no time for an argument.

They guide everyone to the surface. Croc disappears before the police arrive, leaving Bruce with more questions than answers—and one less reason to call him a monster.

`}, 178: {date:'GOTHAM · CASE FILE 26',title:'The last tea party',villain:'hatter',scene:'WINTER GARDEN',caption:'THE CLOCK STOPS HERE',text:`

The Mad Hatter’s elaborate set is built around a greenhouse clock. The people he drew into his fantasy are scared, confused, and ready to choose their own way home.

Bruce keeps his voice calm and the room bright. The spell ends not with a punch, but with each guest remembering their own name.

`}, 179: {date:'GOTHAM · CASE FILE 27',title:'A cure is not a cure',villain:'freeze',scene:'GOTHAM MEDICAL',caption:'HOPE NEEDS MORE THAN ICE',text:`

Victor’s power cell is recovered before the laboratory fails. The research is imperfect, but the doctors find a safer path to keep Nora stable while they continue their work.

Fries surrenders without a fight. Bruce sees a future case that may not need to be a battle at all.

`}, 180: {date:'GOTHAM · CASE FILE 28',title:'The city wakes',villain:'bane',scene:'GOTHAM ROOFTOPS',caption:'DAWN OVER THE NARROWS',text:`

Bane’s final move is a coordinated strike meant to make Gotham believe resistance is pointless. Instead, neighbors open doors, medics share supplies, and officers protect the evacuation routes.

Bruce faces Bane after the last civilians are safe. Strength matters, but it is not the only strength in the city.

`}, 181: {date:'GOTHAM · BEFORE DAWN',title:'A place to begin',scene:'WAYNE CAVE',caption:'ONE PROMISE. ONE FIRST STEP.',text:'

Alfred has left the gear ready: the field guide on the bench, prototypes on the armor table, the suit in its display frame, and the Batmobile resting beneath the stone ceiling. The elevator waits at the far end of the cave. Nothing here is finished, and nobody pretends otherwise.

Bruce takes in the quiet workshop and the steady lights. Beyond the cave lies a city full of strangers, each with a story he cannot know yet. He cannot undo the night that changed his life. He can choose what he does with the nights still ahead.

One man. One promise. A first step into the dark.

Explore the cave, inspect every piece of equipment, collect Riddler trophies, and take the elevator when you are ready.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Expand the existing Batman story game to about 40 chapters with cinematic scenes, Riddler trophies, a visible grappling gun, and the requested villains.

## Requirements
- Preserve existing game and story content while expanding to about 40 beats.
- Include Joker, Bane, Riddler, Two-Face, Killer Croc, Mad Hatter, and Mr. Freeze.
- Keep trophy collection optional for cave progression; reveal the grappling-gun model when its pickup is collected.

## Decisions
- Use villain-specific styling for story scene cards.
- Trophy collectibles do not block cave progression.
- Grappling gun is holstered on Batman and appears after pickup.

## Work State
### Completed
- Expanded the story to exactly 40 beats; the later case files feature all requested villains.
- Added five glowing question-mark trophy pickups and a HUD counter.
- Added the holstered grappling-gun model and pickup reveal behavior.
- Connected beat metadata to the scene card in `renderBeat()` (villain styling, scene tag, and caption).
- Verified inline module syntax with `node --check /tmp/opencode/index.mjs` and confirmed 40 story beats and five trophy entries.

### Active
- Browser-test the game, including scene cards, progression, trophy pickup/counting, and grapple pickup/model visibility.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Browser-test the story presentation and gameplay interactions.
2. Fix any issues found and rerun syntax/count checks.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Story beats, scene-card rendering, cave collectibles, HUD, Batman model, and grapple behavior.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; `index.html` is the only known modified file.
- The grapple action is combat-only and uses `G`; its gameplay function predates the visible model.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Make the Batman game have 40 genuinely playable chapters, preserving the origin content and featuring requested villains in gameplay.
- Keep the existing cave and game content while adding chapter progression and encounters.

## Requirements
- Preserve the origin as the beginning, followed by playable chapters and villain encounters.
- Include Joker, Bane, Riddler, Two-Face, Killer Croc, Mad Hatter, and Mr. Freeze as in-game villains.
- Riddler trophies remain optional; reveal the grapple-gun model after pickup.
- Story cards alone do not count as playable chapters.

## Decisions
- Retain the origin story cards and cave as the opening, then progress into playable encounters.
- Treat the existing generic East End fight and Black Mask encounter as insufficient on their own.
- Use chapter-specific objectives and named bosses, with a completion overlay intended to advance between chapters.

## Work State
### Completed
- Expanded the case-file story cards and added five optional cave trophies, a counter, and a grapple-gun pickup model.
- Browser-tested story navigation, cave pickups, trophy counting, grapple visibility, and entry to combat in earlier work.
- Added `#chapterClear` overlay markup and styling.
- Added a chapter-data array with named missions, locations, objectives, and bosses; it currently contains 39 entries, not the required 40.
- Updated enemy creation to give villain bosses distinct colors and visual details.
- Updated combat startup and completion to use chapter data and show the chapter-clear overlay after winning.

### Active
- Finish and verify the 40-chapter playable progression.
- Connect the chapter-clear button to advance into the next chapter and ensure the final chapter ends appropriately.
- Make villain encounters and objectives function reliably across chapter resets; inspect/update HUD text that still references Black Mask.
- Browser-test chapter progression, combat, and villain encounters.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect `index.html` for remaining old Black Mask-specific combat logic and verify chapter setup/reset behavior.
2. Add the missing 40th chapter and wire `#nextChapter` to advance or finish the story.
3. Browser-test the full chapter flow and each requested villain encounter.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game, story cards, cave pickups, combat systems, chapter data, and new chapter-clear overlay.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; `index.html` is the only known modified file.
- The chapter array currently has 39 entries, including the East End opener.
- `#nextChapter` exists, but no click handler has yet been added.
- `updateCombatHud()` and other legacy combat UI may still use Black Mask labels.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Make the Batman game have 40 genuinely playable chapters, preserving the origin content and featuring requested villains in gameplay.
- Keep the existing cave and game content while adding chapter progression and encounters.

## Requirements
- Preserve the origin as the beginning, followed by playable chapters and villain encounters.
- Include Joker, Bane, Riddler, Two-Face, Killer Croc, Mad Hatter, and Mr. Freeze as in-game villains.
- Riddler trophies remain optional; reveal the grapple-gun model after pickup.
- Story cards alone do not count as playable chapters.

## Decisions
- Retain the origin story cards and cave as the opening, then progress into playable encounters.
- Use chapter-specific objectives and named bosses, with a completion overlay to advance between chapters.

## Work State
### Completed
- Expanded the case-file story cards and added five optional cave trophies, a counter, and a grapple-gun pickup model.
- Added villain-specific boss visuals, combat objectives, and chapter completion overlay.
- Added chapter progression with a continue button and final-story ending.
- Expanded the playable chapter data to 40 entries; verified all requested villain names are included.
- Updated chapter HUD labels and combat reset behavior; `node --check /tmp/opencode/game-check.mjs` passed.

### Active
- Browser-test chapter progression, combat resets, and the requested villain encounters.
- Check that the existing combat flow and chapter numbering behave correctly from the cave through the final chapter.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Browser-test cave entry, chapter completion/advance, retry, and final ending.
2. Verify named bosses and HUD labels during combat, including repeated chapter resets.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game, story cards, cave pickups, combat systems, 40-chapter data, and progression UI.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; `index.html` is modified.
- The cave is the prologue; playable chapters are numbered 01–40.
- Syntax was checked after extracting the module script to `/tmp/opencode/game-check.mjs`; browser testing remains pending.
