Begin with the book.'] 208: ]; 209: function startDialogue(lines){dialogueQueue=lines.map(([s,t])=>({s,t}));dialogueBusy=true;$('#dialogue').classList.add('show');nextLine()} 210: function nextLine(){if(!dialogueQueue.length){dialogueBusy=false;$('#dialogue').classList.remove('show');return}let d=dialogueQueue.shift();$('#speaker').textContent=d.s;$('#line').textContent='“'+d.t+'”'} 211: $('#dialogue').addEventListener('pointerdown',nextLine);addEventListener('keydown',e=>{if(e.key==='Enter'){if(dialogueBusy)nextLine();else if($('#story').classList.contains('show'))$('#storyNext').click()}}); 212: const storyBeats=[ 213: {date:'GOTHAM CITY · 1982',title:'A night at the movies',text:'

Gotham’s old theater empties into a rain-bright street. Thomas and Martha Wayne walk home with their young son, Bruce, still talking about the film. His mother holds his hand; his father listens as if the story matters as much as the night is beautiful.

Their shortcut passes a narrow alley. A stranger steps from the dark and asks for money. Thomas does not reach for a weapon or shout. He gives the gunman $200—everything he has—and tries to make himself the only danger in the alley.

“Take it. Just let my family go.”

For one suspended second, the city seems to hold its breath.

'}, 214: {date:'GOTHAM CITY · THAT NIGHT',title:'The promise',text:'

The gunshot cracks across the street. Thomas and Martha fall beneath the streetlamp. Bruce is left kneeling beside them, surrounded by a city that keeps moving but will never look the same to him again.

In the weeks that follow, adults speak softly around him. They tell him he is safe now, that the police will find the killer, that time will make the pain smaller. None of those words can bring his parents back. Bruce learns that helplessness can feel louder than any siren.

Grief hardens into a promise—not a plan yet, only a vow he will carry into every room: no one else should have to feel this alone.

'}, 215: {date:'WAYNE MANOR · THE YEARS AFTER',title:'A house full of echoes',text:'

The manor is enormous, but after the funeral it feels too quiet. Bruce grows up among portraits, locked rooms, and the careful kindness of the family’s longtime butler, Alfred Pennyworth. Alfred makes breakfast, remembers birthdays, and never asks Bruce to pretend he is all right.

Bruce studies, travels, and searches for a way to understand the violence that took his parents. He learns how fear works, how people survive, and how easily a powerful family can mistake its own comfort for the health of its city.

The promise stays with him. It changes shape as he does: first a child’s wish, then a question, and finally a responsibility he cannot hand to anyone else.

'}, 216: {date:'GOTHAM CITY · 2008',title:'A fortune, a house, a name',text:'

Twenty-six years later, Bruce uncovers a fortune his father had quietly set aside—seed money for a plan Thomas never finished. Bruce invests it, buys back a neglected mansion, and gives the work a public name: Wayne Enterprises.

From the outside, it looks like a return to the life he was born to lead. The grand rooms fill with donors, champagne, and polished promises. Harvey Dent, Gotham’s tireless district attorney, is among the guests. He believes the city can be repaired through courage and honest institutions.

Bruce admires that conviction. He also knows how many people are waiting for someone else to fix things. Behind the parties, he begins asking harder questions about what a single person can do.

'}, 217: {date:'GOTHAM CITY · 2009',title:'The cost of hope',text:'

A year later, a terrible incident leaves Harvey Dent’s face scarred and his life changed. The city’s bright public hope is suddenly vulnerable to pain, anger, and the cruel appetite of headlines. Bruce watches the damage from a distance and recognizes the same old feeling: the moment when safety proves it was never guaranteed.

He retreats from the parties and the easy explanations. With a bag in hand, he descends beneath Wayne Manor into a forgotten cave. The stone is cold, the passages are rough, and the darkness seems almost honest. Here, at least, nobody asks him to smile for a photograph.

For a while, Bruce tells himself solitude is the same thing as purpose.

'}, 218: {date:'WAYNE CAVE · THE FIRST VISIT',title:'A man in the dark',text:'

“Excuse me, sir. Are you looking for something?” an old man calls from the cave entrance. “There’s nothing in here. It’s old—just like me.”

Bruce bristles. “I’m trying to do something with this place. What makes you think you can tell me what to do?” The stranger does not rise to the challenge. He simply points out that Bruce is standing on private property and waits for him to answer.

Bruce refuses to leave. The old man gives him one last look and walks away. The exchange is awkward, almost absurd, but it stays with Bruce. Someone has finally spoken to him plainly, without fear of his name or his money.

'}, 219: {date:'WAYNE CAVE · THREE MONTHS LATER',title:'The long quiet',text:'

Days pass. Bruce returns to the cave with tools, then with plans, then with nothing but questions. He measures the cavern and marks out possible work areas. He tries to turn the rock into a headquarters by force of will, but every task exposes another one he does not know how to do.

Above him, the manor continues its routines. Below, the cave answers with drips of water and the occasional flutter of wings. Bruce begins to understand that a mission built alone may only become another way to hide.

One evening he hears footsteps at the entrance. The same old man has come back. This time, he is carrying a thermos and a small stack of notes.

'}, 220: {date:'WAYNE CAVE · A RETURN',title:'An unexpected ally',text:'

“Excuse me, sir. Remember me?” The man sets down the thermos. “I’m Alfred.” Bruce has known him all his life, of course, but down here they meet differently: not as employer and servant, nor as grieving boy and patient guardian, but as two people looking at the same unfinished room.

Alfred has sketched a workbench, a computer station, and a safer route back to the house. He has also found a book on self-defense. Bruce studies the pages and recognizes how much he does not know. Alfred does not gloat. He pours tea.

“You’ll need more than determination, sir,” he says. “Determination is what gets you to the door. Preparation is what gets you home.”

'}, 221: {date:'WAYNE CAVE · THE PLAN TAKES SHAPE',title:'Tools, not answers',text:'

They work in fits and starts. Alfred knows how to keep a project moving; Bruce knows how to ask questions that make the project bigger. The computer station becomes a place to sort reports and maps. A suit bay takes shape against the stone. The elevator connects the cave to the estate without sending either man through the front hall.

Every object has a purpose and a limit. Batarangs can distract or disarm, but they cannot make a bad decision wise. Smoke pellets can cover a retreat, but they cannot turn a retreat into a victory. A grapple prototype can bridge a gap only if the person using it thinks before leaping.

Bruce begins to see the cave not as a lair, but as a workshop for learning how to help.

'}, 222: {date:'WAYNE CAVE · THE VEHICLE BAY',title:'A machine with sharp edges',text:'

The car is the most ambitious piece of the plan and the least finished. Its armored panels catch the work lights; its engine answers a test with a growl that makes dust fall from the ceiling. Alfred circles it with a clipboard, noting what still needs attention.

“It’s not quite street legal,” he says. “And I would avoid the red switch.” Bruce asks if it is safe. Alfred considers the question for a beat too long. They agree to call it a prototype and to keep the first test somewhere far from traffic.

The machine represents possibility, but also temptation: the urge to make an entrance instead of doing the patient work. Bruce closes the hood. Tonight, the car can wait.

'}, 223: {date:'WAYNE CAVE · BEFORE DAWN',title:'The first lesson',text:'

Alfred lays the self-defense field guide on the workbench. It is not as impressive as the suit, the car, or the glowing computer screens. Its pages are worn at the corners, full of diagrams and notes in Alfred’s neat hand. Bruce opens it carefully.

“Begin with the book,” Alfred tells him. “Learn how to keep your balance. Learn when to move, when to listen, and when walking away is the bravest thing you can do.” Bruce looks toward the equipment waiting around the cave. For the first time, it feels less like a collection of answers and more like a list of responsibilities.

There is still a long way to go. But the work has finally begun.

'}, 224: {date:'GOTHAM · CASE FILE 01',title:'The question in the dark',villain:'riddler',scene:'THE NARROWS',caption:'A QUESTION WITH NO ANSWER',text:`

A green question mark is painted on the shutter of a closed pawnshop. Bruce photographs it from across the street. It is not a confession—just the first hint that someone wants the city to know he is watching.

Alfred finds a string of riddles in old police reports. Bruce files them away, unsure whether the author is a criminal, a prankster, or both.

`}, 225: {date:'GOTHAM · CASE FILE 02',title:'A smile on the wire',villain:'joker',scene:'GOTHAM BROADCAST',caption:'LAUGHTER AFTER MIDNIGHT',text:`

Every screen in a downtown electronics shop flickers to life at once. A pale face smiles through the static, telling a joke no one in the room finds funny. The broadcast ends with a burst of confetti and a list of abandoned buildings.

Bruce watches the recording twice. The danger is not the punchline. It is how carefully the speaker studied his audience.

`}, 226: {date:'GOTHAM · CASE FILE 03',title:'The coin that never lands',villain:'twoface',scene:'OLD COURTHOUSE',caption:'JUSTICE ON BOTH SIDES',text:`

Harvey Dent once believed a fair trial could change Gotham. Now a scarred former prosecutor lets a coin decide which version of justice will speak for him. One side is bright; the other is dark and worn.

Bruce keeps Harvey’s old campaign button beside the case notes. He will not reduce his friend to the damage done to him.

`}, 227: {date:'GOTHAM · CASE FILE 04',title:'Something beneath the river',villain:'croc',scene:'EAST END DRAINS',caption:'EYES BELOW THE WATER',text:`

Workers refuse to enter a storm tunnel after hearing heavy footsteps beneath the grates. A hulking figure is seen only in the ripples and the brief flash of yellow eyes.

The newspapers call him a monster. Bruce writes a different question in the margin: what happened to the boy before the city gave him that name?

`}, 228: {date:'GOTHAM · CASE FILE 05',title:'The tea-party invitation',villain:'hatter',scene:'ABANDONED THEATER',caption:'ONE SEAT LEFT EMPTY',text:`

In a derelict playhouse, a tiny paper invitation waits on a velvet chair. It promises a perfect world to anyone willing to follow the White Rabbit. The ink is fresh; the theater has been empty for years.

Bruce recognizes the language of a trap dressed as comfort. Some people do not want power over a city. They want power over one person at a time.

`}, 229: {date:'GOTHAM · CASE FILE 06',title:'The cold front',villain:'freeze',scene:'GOTHAM HARBOR',caption:'WINTER IN THE WRONG SEASON',text:`

A shipment of medical equipment disappears from a waterfront laboratory. Frost feathers the inside of a locked storage door, though the night outside is warm.

The lead points to Victor Fries, a scientist trying to keep his wife alive. Bruce marks the name carefully. A desperate motive does not make dangerous methods harmless.

`}, 230: {date:'GOTHAM · CASE FILE 07',title:'The man who broke a wall',villain:'bane',scene:'BLACKGATE PRISON',caption:'STRENGTH IS A STRATEGY',text:`

A transfer report describes a prisoner who studies every guard rotation and every weakness in the building. Bane does not waste strength; he saves it for the moment it matters.

Bruce adds endurance drills to his training. Winning a fight, he realizes, may begin long before the first blow.

`}, 231: {date:'GOTHAM · CASE FILE 08',title:'The clown’s calling card',villain:'joker',scene:'MONTOYA CIRCUS',caption:'THE SHOW WILL GO ON',text:`

A shuttered circus tent is found ringed with playing cards. Somewhere inside, a music box turns by itself. The officers who enter hear applause from an empty grandstand.

Bruce studies the scene photographs. The performer wants fear, but he also wants an audience. That need may be the most dangerous clue of all.

`}, 232: {date:'GOTHAM · CASE FILE 09',title:'A city-sized puzzle',villain:'riddler',scene:'FINANCIAL DISTRICT',caption:'FOLLOW THE GREEN LIGHT',text:`

Traffic signals across three blocks change in a sequence that spells out a riddle. The pattern leads to a locked service room—and a second riddle hidden inside it.

Bruce maps the route without entering the buildings. Whoever designed the game is testing patience as much as intelligence.

`}, 233: {date:'GOTHAM · CASE FILE 10',title:'Harvey’s other face',villain:'twoface',scene:'GOTHAM CENTRAL',caption:'A COIN IN THE EVIDENCE ROOM',text:`

A witness refuses to testify after receiving a silver coin with a scorched edge. Harvey’s old colleagues want to protect him from the investigation; Harvey would have demanded the truth.

Bruce asks Alfred to keep the original case files safe. Memory can preserve a person’s best self, even when the present tries to erase it.

`}, 234: {date:'GOTHAM · CASE FILE 11',title:'The king below',villain:'croc',scene:'OLD SEWER LINE',caption:'THE TUNNELS HAVE A KING',text:`

A missing-persons report leads to a forgotten passage beneath the river. The marks on the concrete are too high for an ordinary man, and the torn steel bars bend outward.

Bruce brings a rescue map to the police instead of charging underground alone. Preparation is not cowardice; it is how you make sure someone comes back.

`}, 235: {date:'GOTHAM · CASE FILE 12',title:'A dream with locked doors',villain:'hatter',scene:'WONDERLAND ROOM',caption:'WAKE UP, GOTHAM',text:`

Several people describe the same impossible tea party, down to the ticking clock and the empty chair. Their accounts point toward a doctor who has learned to make fantasy feel safer than waking life.

Bruce begins reading about coercion and trauma. The mind is not a puzzle box to force open. A victim needs a way out, not another person holding the key.

`}, 236: {date:'GOTHAM · CASE FILE 13',title:'A promise in the ice',villain:'freeze',scene:'CRYOGENICS LAB',caption:'LOVE FROZEN IN TIME',text:`

Victor Fries leaves a message asking for a single component to stabilize Nora’s chamber. It is the first time his trail sounds less like a threat and more like a plea.

Bruce asks Wayne Medical to review the research. There may be a way to help without letting a desperate man endanger anyone else.

`}, 237: {date:'GOTHAM · CASE FILE 14',title:'Bane’s careful silence',villain:'bane',scene:'PORT ADAMS',caption:'THE STRONGEST MAN WAITS',text:`

A crate of experimental medical supplies vanishes from the port. The theft is clean, with no broken locks and no witnesses willing to talk. Bane has made the city look in the wrong direction.

Bruce studies the timing. A patient opponent can turn a city’s routines into a weapon.

`}, 238: {date:'GOTHAM · CASE FILE 15',title:'The punchline is a warning',villain:'joker',scene:'PARK ROW',caption:'NO ONE IS LAUGHING',text:`

At a charity hall, the lights go out for eleven seconds. When they return, every guest has a paper smile on the table and the donation ledger is gone. No one is hurt, but the message is unmistakable.

Bruce asks the staff what they saw before asking what they lost. Fear makes people forget that their safety matters more than a ledger.

`}, 239: {date:'GOTHAM · CASE FILE 16',title:'Riddles on the rooftops',villain:'riddler',scene:'ROOFTOP GRID',caption:'THE NEXT CLUE IS ABOVE YOU',text:`

Green markers appear on rooftops overlooking the financial district. Each one points to a place where Gotham failed someone: a shuttered clinic, an empty school, a neglected shelter.

Bruce sees the cruelty inside the cleverness. The Riddler may know the city’s wounds, but he treats them as props in a game.

`}, 240: {date:'GOTHAM · CASE FILE 17',title:'The courthouse divided',villain:'twoface',scene:'GOTHAM COURTHOUSE',caption:'ONE VERDICT, TWO OUTCOMES',text:`

Harvey sends a sealed envelope to Bruce. Inside is a list of people he wants protected from his own gang. The handwriting shifts from careful to jagged halfway down the page.

Bruce does not mistake the letter for an apology. He sees it as a chance to keep innocent people out of the crossfire.

`}, 241: {date:'GOTHAM · CASE FILE 18',title:'The river remembers',villain:'croc',scene:'FLOODED UNDERPASS',caption:'A RESCUE IN THE DARK',text:`

Rising water traps a maintenance crew in a tunnel. Something moves beneath the surface, then lifts a steel gate from its hinges. The workers emerge shaken but alive.

Bruce cannot tell whether Croc saved them or simply cleared his path. Either way, the next search will need a boat, a plan, and a team.

`}, 242: {date:'GOTHAM · CASE FILE 19',title:'The clockwork rabbit',villain:'hatter',scene:'CLOCKTOWER',caption:'TIME IS RUNNING OUT',text:`

A clocktower chimes thirteen times. A trail of brass gears leads to a locked room where a frightened witness has been hidden in plain sight.

Alfred reminds Bruce that rescuing someone means listening to them after the danger passes. The exit is only the beginning of feeling safe again.

`}, 243: {date:'GOTHAM · CASE FILE 20',title:'Whiteout at the docks',villain:'freeze',scene:'GOTHAM DOCKS',caption:'THE HARBOR TURNS TO GLASS',text:`

A wave of freezing mist crawls across the docks as Victor tries to retrieve a power cell. Workers are stranded behind the ice, too afraid to cross the slick metal walkways.

Bruce coordinates a safe evacuation with the harbor crew. He will face Fries if he must, but the people in danger come first.

`}, 244: {date:'GOTHAM · CASE FILE 21',title:'A test of endurance',villain:'bane',scene:'NARROWS ROOFLINE',caption:'NO SHORTCUT THROUGH FEAR',text:`

Bane leaves a trail of staged emergencies across the Narrows. Each one forces responders to split their attention. The trap is not a single fight; it is exhaustion.

Bruce changes the plan: call in help, rotate teams, and refuse to let pride set the pace. The city is stronger when no one has to carry it alone.

`}, 245: {date:'GOTHAM · CASE FILE 22',title:'The joker takes the stage',villain:'joker',scene:'MONTOYA PLAYHOUSE',caption:'THE HOUSE LIGHTS GO OUT',text:`

The old playhouse is filled with laughing recordings and painted spotlights. The Joker wants the entire city to watch his performance, but the people inside are not an audience—they are hostages.

Bruce studies the exits first. A dramatic entrance can wait until everyone has a way out.

`}, 246: {date:'GOTHAM · CASE FILE 23',title:'The answer beneath the question',villain:'riddler',scene:'WAYNE STATION',caption:'EVERY CLUE LEAVES A TRACE',text:`

A final riddle points to a substation carrying power to a hospital. Bruce spots the hidden override before the lights go out and alerts the engineers.

The puzzle is solved, but the lesson is larger: cleverness without care can become another kind of cruelty.

`}, 247: {date:'GOTHAM · CASE FILE 24',title:'A chance for Harvey',villain:'twoface',scene:'ACE CHEMICALS',caption:'THE COIN FALLS',text:`

Harvey’s crew corners a bookkeeper who once helped build his career. The coin spins across a catwalk and lands on the scarred side. Bruce steps between them before the verdict can become irreversible.

He speaks to Harvey by name, not by nickname. One honest voice cannot undo everything, but it can leave a door open.

`}, 248: {date:'GOTHAM · CASE FILE 25',title:'A truce in the tunnels',villain:'croc',scene:'UNDERCITY',caption:'THE WAY OUT IS TOGETHER',text:`

Bruce finds Croc guarding a group of unhoused people from a collapsing tunnel. Neither trusts the other, but the roof is coming down and there is no time for an argument.

They guide everyone to the surface. Croc disappears before the police arrive, leaving Bruce with more questions than answers—and one less reason to call him a monster.

`}, 249: {date:'GOTHAM · CASE FILE 26',title:'The last tea party',villain:'hatter',scene:'WINTER GARDEN',caption:'THE CLOCK STOPS HERE',text:`

The Mad Hatter’s elaborate set is built around a greenhouse clock. The people he drew into his fantasy are scared, confused, and ready to choose their own way home.

Bruce keeps his voice calm and the room bright. The spell ends not with a punch, but with each guest remembering their own name.

`}, 250: {date:'GOTHAM · CASE FILE 27',title:'A cure is not a cure',villain:'freeze',scene:'GOTHAM MEDICAL',caption:'HOPE NEEDS MORE THAN ICE',text:`

Victor’s power cell is recovered before the laboratory fails. The research is imperfect, but the doctors find a safer path to keep Nora stable while they continue their work.

Fries surrenders without a fight. Bruce sees a future case that may not need to be a battle at all.

`}, 251: {date:'GOTHAM · CASE FILE 28',title:'The city wakes',villain:'bane',scene:'GOTHAM ROOFTOPS',caption:'DAWN OVER THE NARROWS',text:`

Bane’s final move is a coordinated strike meant to make Gotham believe resistance is pointless. Instead, neighbors open doors, medics share supplies, and officers protect the evacuation routes.

Bruce faces Bane after the last civilians are safe. Strength matters, but it is not the only strength in the city.

`}, 252: {date:'GOTHAM · BEFORE DAWN',title:'A place to begin',scene:'WAYNE CAVE',caption:'ONE PROMISE. ONE FIRST STEP.',text:'

Alfred has left the gear ready: the field guide on the bench, prototypes on the armor table, the suit in its display frame, and the Batmobile resting beneath the stone ceiling. The elevator waits at the far end of the cave. Nothing here is finished, and nobody pretends otherwise.

Bruce takes in the quiet workshop and the steady lights. Beyond the cave lies a city full of strangers, each with a story he cannot know yet. He cannot undo the night that changed his life. He can choose what he does with the nights still ahead.

One man. One promise. A first step into the dark.

Explore the cave, inspect every piece of equipment, collect Riddler trophies, and take the elevator when you are ready.

## Objective
- Expand and polish the Batman game into a story with playable chapters, retaining the origin and cave prologue while improving characters, movement, and Batmobile driving.

## Requirements
- Keep the origin first, followed by playable chapters and villain encounters; story cards alone do not count as playable chapters.
- Include Joker, Bane, Riddler, Two-Face, Killer Croc, Mad Hatter, and Mr. Freeze.
- Keep Riddler trophies optional and reveal the grapple-gun model after pickup.
- Give short villains normal height, characters visible faces, Batman walking motion, substantial plot twists before villain fights, and drivable Batmobile controls.

## Decisions
- Retain the origin story cards and cave as the prologue, followed by playable encounters.
- Use chapter-specific objectives and named bosses, with a completion overlay to advance between chapters.

## Work State
### Completed
- Expanded the case-file story cards and added five optional cave trophies, a counter, and a grapple-gun pickup model.
- Added villain-specific boss visuals, combat objectives, chapter completion overlay, and chapter progression.
- Added 40 uniquely named playable chapter entries, including every requested villain.
- Updated chapter HUD labels, boss display, combat reset behavior, retry action, and final-story ending.
- Added Batman limb pivot groups (`legPivots`, `armPivots`) and Batmobile wheel references (`carWheels`) as groundwork for animation and driving.
- Repositioned the cave Batmobile and interaction marker to `(7, …, -5)` and moved its label to match.
- Added shared enemy face materials and meshes for eyes, pupils, noses, and mouths.

### Active
- Wire `legPivots` and `armPivots` into movement animation, with clean idle-pose resets.
- Scale short villains independently of boss-wide scaling.
- Replace generic pre-boss dialogue with substantial, chapter-specific twists.
- Implement Batmobile enter/exit and driving; it remains a cave display model.
- Verify syntax, `git diff --check`, and gameplay across the prologue and chapters.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Add individual short-villain scaling without shrinking all bosses.
2. Animate Batman’s limb pivots while moving and reset them while idle.
3. Add chapter-specific twist dialogue before villain fights.
4. Implement Batmobile enter/exit and driving controls, using `carWheels` as appropriate.
5. Verify syntax, diffs, and the complete gameplay flow.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game scene, character and vehicle models, chapter data, dialogue, controls, combat, and progression UI.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; `index.html` is modified.
- Cave is the prologue; playable chapters are numbered 01–40.
- Boss arrival dialogue in `hitEnemy` and most chapter introductions in `startCombat` remain generic.

183:   'The shopkeeper hid a ledger beneath the counter: Black Mask’s crew are collecting rents for a block that was condemned years ago, and the real target is the tenants’ deed archive.',
184:   'The studio feed is not a ransom broadcast. Joker is using the emergency override to expose a police dispatch channel, and the voice directing the crew is a fake loop.',
185:   'Harvey’s coin was planted at the courthouse before the ambush. The clerk who reported it is protecting the real witness, Harvey’s former investigator, who found the original evidence was altered.',
186:   'Croc did not flood the tunnel to trap the workers. He broke the gate to divert a chemical spill from them, and the current is carrying a second, more dangerous leak toward the river.',
187:   'The captives were never meant to be an audience. Hatter’s tea-party recording is masking their calls for help, while the theater manager quietly left a trail of real exit marks.',
188:   'Freeze’s rig is not aimed at the harbor. Its stolen regulator is keeping a failing hospital freezer stable; the dock attack is a cover to retrieve the only replacement cell.',
189:   'Bane’s escape is a decoy. He has arranged for the guards to chase him while his crew moves a prison transport carrying a witness who can identify the buyers of the stolen supplies.',
190:   'The circus explosives are theatrical. Joker’s real trap is the crowd-control system, which will lock every exit when the lights return; one performer has secretly sabotaged the trigger.',
191:   'Riddler’s rooftop relay is broadcasting the city’s neglected addresses, not a bomb code. He wants to force an evacuation, but his map includes a shelter whose residents cannot be moved safely.',
192:   'The ambush report came from inside Gotham Central. Harvey’s crew is targeting a sealed evidence locker because it contains proof that an officer sold his old case notes.',
193:   'Croc has been leaving food and dry blankets near the sewer markers. The missing crew followed those signs to safety, while someone else has been using Croc’s name to empty the tunnels.',
194:   'The maze’s clues are in the captives’ own handwriting. Hatter has been copying their memories to make them doubt which doors are real; one victim has marked the true route in reverse.',
195:   'Freeze’s lab sample is a decoy with Victor’s serial number. Someone copied his research to frame him, and the genuine cryogenic unit is already being moved through the ventilation level.',
196:   'Bane’s crew stole medical supplies to treat injured dockworkers after a staged crane collapse. The collapse was deliberate, but the orders came from a buyer trying to erase the workers’ testimony.',
197:   'The paper smiles carry no threat. Joker has hidden the charity ledger inside the lighting rig because it records a quiet payoff to the person who disabled the hall alarms.',
198:   'The rooftop markers form a route to an abandoned clinic. Riddler found records proving the city closed it despite a funded repair grant—and someone pocketed the money.',
199:   'Harvey’s sealed list is a real warning, not a trap. One of the witnesses has been feeding both sides false names to provoke a shootout and destroy the case files.',
200:   'The workers are already above water. Croc has gone back below to hold a damaged floodgate shut, and the timed bursts are his warning that the tunnel is about to fail.',
201:   'The thirteenth chime is an old emergency signal, not Hatter’s countdown. The hidden witness is helping him keep a child safe from a pursuer who followed them into the tower.',

Gotham’s old theater empties into a rain-bright street. Thomas and Martha Wayne walk home with their young son, Bruce, still talking about the film. His mother holds his hand; his father listens as if the story matters as much as the night is beautiful.

Their shortcut passes a narrow alley. A stranger steps from the dark and asks for money. Thomas does not reach for a weapon or shout. He gives the gunman $200—everything he has—and tries to make himself the only danger in the alley.

“Take it. Just let my family go.”

For one suspended second, the city seems to hold its breath.

'}, 256: {date:'GOTHAM CITY · THAT NIGHT',title:'The promise',text:'

The gunshot cracks across the street. Thomas and Martha fall beneath the streetlamp. Bruce is left kneeling beside them, surrounded by a city that keeps moving but will never look the same to him again.

In the weeks that follow, adults speak softly around him. They tell him he is safe now, that the police will find the killer, that time will make the pain smaller. None of those words can bring his parents back. Bruce learns that helplessness can feel louder than any siren.

Grief hardens into a promise—not a plan yet, only a vow he will carry into every room: no one else should have to feel this alone.

'}, 257: {date:'WAYNE MANOR · THE YEARS AFTER',title:'A house full of echoes',text:'

The manor is enormous, but after the funeral it feels too quiet. Bruce grows up among portraits, locked rooms, and the careful kindness of the family’s longtime butler, Alfred Pennyworth. Alfred makes breakfast, remembers birthdays, and never asks Bruce to pretend he is all right.

Bruce studies, travels, and searches for a way to understand the violence that took his parents. He learns how fear works, how people survive, and how easily a powerful family can mistake its own comfort for the health of its city.

The promise stays with him. It changes shape as he does: first a child’s wish, then a question, and finally a responsibility he cannot hand to anyone else.

'}, 258: {date:'GOTHAM CITY · 2008',title:'A fortune, a house, a name',text:'

Twenty-six years later, Bruce uncovers a fortune his father had quietly set aside—seed money for a plan Thomas never finished. Bruce invests it, buys back a neglected mansion, and gives the work a public name: Wayne Enterprises.

From the outside, it looks like a return to the life he was born to lead. The grand rooms fill with donors, champagne, and polished promises. Harvey Dent, Gotham’s tireless district attorney, is among the guests. He believes the city can be repaired through courage and honest institutions.

Bruce admires that conviction. He also knows how many people are waiting for someone else to fix things. Behind the parties, he begins asking harder questions about what a single person can do.

'}, 259: {date:'GOTHAM CITY · 2009',title:'The cost of hope',text:'

A year later, a terrible incident leaves Harvey Dent’s face scarred and his life changed. The city’s bright public hope is suddenly vulnerable to pain, anger, and the cruel appetite of headlines. Bruce watches the damage from a distance and recognizes the same old feeling: the moment when safety proves it was never guaranteed.

He retreats from the parties and the easy explanations. With a bag in hand, he descends beneath Wayne Manor into a forgotten cave. The stone is cold, the passages are rough, and the darkness seems almost honest. Here, at least, nobody asks him to smile for a photograph.

For a while, Bruce tells himself solitude is the same thing as purpose.

'}, 260: {date:'WAYNE CAVE · THE FIRST VISIT',title:'A man in the dark',text:'

“Excuse me, sir. Are you looking for something?” an old man calls from the cave entrance. “There’s nothing in here. It’s old—just like me.”

Bruce bristles. “I’m trying to do something with this place. What makes you think you can tell me what to do?” The stranger does not rise to the challenge. He simply points out that Bruce is standing on private property and waits for him to answer.

Bruce refuses to leave. The old man gives him one last look and walks away. The exchange is awkward, almost absurd, but it stays with Bruce. Someone has finally spoken to him plainly, without fear of his name or his money.

'}, 261: {date:'WAYNE CAVE · THREE MONTHS LATER',title:'The long quiet',text:'

Days pass. Bruce returns to the cave with tools, then with plans, then with nothing but questions. He measures the cavern and marks out possible work areas. He tries to turn the rock into a headquarters by force of will, but every task exposes another one he does not know how to do.

Above him, the manor continues its routines. Below, the cave answers with drips of water and the occasional flutter of wings. Bruce begins to understand that a mission built alone may only become another way to hide.

One evening he hears footsteps at the entrance. The same old man has come back. This time, he is carrying a thermos and a small stack of notes.

'}, 262: {date:'WAYNE CAVE · A RETURN',title:'An unexpected ally',text:'

“Excuse me, sir. Remember me?” The man sets down the thermos. “I’m Alfred.” Bruce has known him all his life, of course, but down here they meet differently: not as employer and servant, nor as grieving boy and patient guardian, but as two people looking at the same unfinished room.

Alfred has sketched a workbench, a computer station, and a safer route back to the house. He has also found a book on self-defense. Bruce studies the pages and recognizes how much he does not know. Alfred does not gloat. He pours tea.

“You’ll need more than determination, sir,” he says. “Determination is what gets you to the door. Preparation is what gets you home.”

'}, 263: {date:'WAYNE CAVE · THE PLAN TAKES SHAPE',title:'Tools, not answers',text:'

They work in fits and starts. Alfred knows how to keep a project moving; Bruce knows how to ask questions that make the project bigger. The computer station becomes a place to sort reports and maps. A suit bay takes shape against the stone. The elevator connects the cave to the estate without sending either man through the front hall.

Every object has a purpose and a limit. Batarangs can distract or disarm, but they cannot make a bad decision wise. Smoke pellets can cover a retreat, but they cannot turn a retreat into a victory. A grapple prototype can bridge a gap only if the person using it thinks before leaping.

Bruce begins to see the cave not as a lair, but as a workshop for learning how to help.

'}, 264: {date:'WAYNE CAVE · THE VEHICLE BAY',title:'A machine with sharp edges',text:'

The car is the most ambitious piece of the plan and the least finished. Its armored panels catch the work lights; its engine answers a test with a growl that makes dust fall from the ceiling. Alfred circles it with a clipboard, noting what still needs attention.

“It’s not quite street legal,” he says. “And I would avoid the red switch.” Bruce asks if it is safe. Alfred considers the question for a beat too long. They agree to call it a prototype and to keep the first test somewhere far from traffic.

The machine represents possibility, but also temptation: the urge to make an entrance instead of doing the patient work. Bruce closes the hood. Tonight, the car can wait.

'}, 265: {date:'WAYNE CAVE · BEFORE DAWN',title:'The first lesson',text:'

Alfred lays the self-defense field guide on the workbench. It is not as impressive as the suit, the car, or the glowing computer screens. Its pages are worn at the corners, full of diagrams and notes in Alfred’s neat hand. Bruce opens it carefully.

“Begin with the book,” Alfred tells him. “Learn how to keep your balance. Learn when to move, when to listen, and when walking away is the bravest thing you can do.” Bruce looks toward the equipment waiting around the cave. For the first time, it feels less like a collection of answers and more like a list of responsibilities.

There is still a long way to go. But the work has finally begun.

'}, 266: {date:'GOTHAM · CASE FILE 01',title:'The question in the dark',villain:'riddler',scene:'THE NARROWS',caption:'A QUESTION WITH NO ANSWER',text:`

A green question mark is painted on the shutter of a closed pawnshop. Bruce photographs it from across the street. It is not a confession—just the first hint that someone wants the city to know he is watching.

Alfred finds a string of riddles in old police reports. Bruce files them away, unsure whether the author is a criminal, a prankster, or both.

`}, 267: {date:'GOTHAM · CASE FILE 02',title:'A smile on the wire',villain:'joker',scene:'GOTHAM BROADCAST',caption:'LAUGHTER AFTER MIDNIGHT',text:`

Every screen in a downtown electronics shop flickers to life at once. A pale face smiles through the static, telling a joke no one in the room finds funny. The broadcast ends with a burst of confetti and a list of abandoned buildings.

Bruce watches the recording twice. The danger is not the punchline. It is how carefully the speaker studied his audience.

`}, 268: {date:'GOTHAM · CASE FILE 03',title:'The coin that never lands',villain:'twoface',scene:'OLD COURTHOUSE',caption:'JUSTICE ON BOTH SIDES',text:`

Harvey Dent once believed a fair trial could change Gotham. Now a scarred former prosecutor lets a coin decide which version of justice will speak for him. One side is bright; the other is dark and worn.

Bruce keeps Harvey’s old campaign button beside the case notes. He will not reduce his friend to the damage done to him.

`}, 269: {date:'GOTHAM · CASE FILE 04',title:'Something beneath the river',villain:'croc',scene:'EAST END DRAINS',caption:'EYES BELOW THE WATER',text:`

Workers refuse to enter a storm tunnel after hearing heavy footsteps beneath the grates. A hulking figure is seen only in the ripples and the brief flash of yellow eyes.

The newspapers call him a monster. Bruce writes a different question in the margin: what happened to the boy before the city gave him that name?

`}, 270: {date:'GOTHAM · CASE FILE 05',title:'The tea-party invitation',villain:'hatter',scene:'ABANDONED THEATER',caption:'ONE SEAT LEFT EMPTY',text:`

In a derelict playhouse, a tiny paper invitation waits on a velvet chair. It promises a perfect world to anyone willing to follow the White Rabbit. The ink is fresh; the theater has been empty for years.

Bruce recognizes the language of a trap dressed as comfort. Some people do not want power over a city. They want power over one person at a time.

`}, 271: {date:'GOTHAM · CASE FILE 06',title:'The cold front',villain:'freeze',scene:'GOTHAM HARBOR',caption:'WINTER IN THE WRONG SEASON',text:`

A shipment of medical equipment disappears from a waterfront laboratory. Frost feathers the inside of a locked storage door, though the night outside is warm.

The lead points to Victor Fries, a scientist trying to keep his wife alive. Bruce marks the name carefully. A desperate motive does not make dangerous methods harmless.

`}, 272: {date:'GOTHAM · CASE FILE 07',title:'The man who broke a wall',villain:'bane',scene:'BLACKGATE PRISON',caption:'STRENGTH IS A STRATEGY',text:`

A transfer report describes a prisoner who studies every guard rotation and every weakness in the building. Bane does not waste strength; he saves it for the moment it matters.

Bruce adds endurance drills to his training. Winning a fight, he realizes, may begin long before the first blow.

`}, 273: {date:'GOTHAM · CASE FILE 08',title:'The clown’s calling card',villain:'joker',scene:'MONTOYA CIRCUS',caption:'THE SHOW WILL GO ON',text:`

A shuttered circus tent is found ringed with playing cards. Somewhere inside, a music box turns by itself. The officers who enter hear applause from an empty grandstand.

Bruce studies the scene photographs. The performer wants fear, but he also wants an audience. That need may be the most dangerous clue of all.

`}, 274: {date:'GOTHAM · CASE FILE 09',title:'A city-sized puzzle',villain:'riddler',scene:'FINANCIAL DISTRICT',caption:'FOLLOW THE GREEN LIGHT',text:`

Traffic signals across three blocks change in a sequence that spells out a riddle. The pattern leads to a locked service room—and a second riddle hidden inside it.

Bruce maps the route without entering the buildings. Whoever designed the game is testing patience as much as intelligence.

`}, 275: {date:'GOTHAM · CASE FILE 10',title:'Harvey’s other face',villain:'twoface',scene:'GOTHAM CENTRAL',caption:'A COIN IN THE EVIDENCE ROOM',text:`

A witness refuses to testify after receiving a silver coin with a scorched edge. Harvey’s old colleagues want to protect him from the investigation; Harvey would have demanded the truth.

Bruce asks Alfred to keep the original case files safe. Memory can preserve a person’s best self, even when the present tries to erase it.

`}, 276: {date:'GOTHAM · CASE FILE 11',title:'The king below',villain:'croc',scene:'OLD SEWER LINE',caption:'THE TUNNELS HAVE A KING',text:`

A missing-persons report leads to a forgotten passage beneath the river. The marks on the concrete are too high for an ordinary man, and the torn steel bars bend outward.

Bruce brings a rescue map to the police instead of charging underground alone. Preparation is not cowardice; it is how you make sure someone comes back.

`}, 277: {date:'GOTHAM · CASE FILE 12',title:'A dream with locked doors',villain:'hatter',scene:'WONDERLAND ROOM',caption:'WAKE UP, GOTHAM',text:`

Several people describe the same impossible tea party, down to the ticking clock and the empty chair. Their accounts point toward a doctor who has learned to make fantasy feel safer than waking life.

Bruce begins reading about coercion and trauma. The mind is not a puzzle box to force open. A victim needs a way out, not another person holding the key.

`}, 278: {date:'GOTHAM · CASE FILE 13',title:'A promise in the ice',villain:'freeze',scene:'CRYOGENICS LAB',caption:'LOVE FROZEN IN TIME',text:`

Victor Fries leaves a message asking for a single component to stabilize Nora’s chamber. It is the first time his trail sounds less like a threat and more like a plea.

Bruce asks Wayne Medical to review the research. There may be a way to help without letting a desperate man endanger anyone else.

`}, 279: {date:'GOTHAM · CASE FILE 14',title:'Bane’s careful silence',villain:'bane',scene:'PORT ADAMS',caption:'THE STRONGEST MAN WAITS',text:`

A crate of experimental medical supplies vanishes from the port. The theft is clean, with no broken locks and no witnesses willing to talk. Bane has made the city look in the wrong direction.

Bruce studies the timing. A patient opponent can turn a city’s routines into a weapon.

`}, 280: {date:'GOTHAM · CASE FILE 15',title:'The punchline is a warning',villain:'joker',scene:'PARK ROW',caption:'NO ONE IS LAUGHING',text:`

At a charity hall, the lights go out for eleven seconds. When they return, every guest has a paper smile on the table and the donation ledger is gone. No one is hurt, but the message is unmistakable.

Bruce asks the staff what they saw before asking what they lost. Fear makes people forget that their safety matters more than a ledger.

`}, 281: {date:'GOTHAM · CASE FILE 16',title:'Riddles on the rooftops',villain:'riddler',scene:'ROOFTOP GRID',caption:'THE NEXT CLUE IS ABOVE YOU',text:`

Green markers appear on rooftops overlooking the financial district. Each one points to a place where Gotham failed someone: a shuttered clinic, an empty school, a neglected shelter.

Bruce sees the cruelty inside the cleverness. The Riddler may know the city’s wounds, but he treats them as props in a game.

`}, 282: {date:'GOTHAM · CASE FILE 17',title:'The courthouse divided',villain:'twoface',scene:'GOTHAM COURTHOUSE',caption:'ONE VERDICT, TWO OUTCOMES',text:`

Harvey sends a sealed envelope to Bruce. Inside is a list of people he wants protected from his own gang. The handwriting shifts from careful to jagged halfway down the page.

Bruce does not mistake the letter for an apology. He sees it as a chance to keep innocent people out of the crossfire.

`}, 283: {date:'GOTHAM · CASE FILE 18',title:'The river remembers',villain:'croc',scene:'FLOODED UNDERPASS',caption:'A RESCUE IN THE DARK',text:`

Rising water traps a maintenance crew in a tunnel. Something moves beneath the surface, then lifts a steel gate from its hinges. The workers emerge shaken but alive.

Bruce cannot tell whether Croc saved them or simply cleared his path. Either way, the next search will need a boat, a plan, and a team.

## Objective
- Expand and polish the Batman game into a story with playable chapters, retaining the origin and cave prologue while improving characters, movement, and Batmobile driving.

## Requirements
- Keep the origin first, followed by playable chapters and villain encounters; story cards alone do not count as playable chapters.
- Include Joker, Bane, Riddler, Two-Face, Killer Croc, Mad Hatter, and Mr. Freeze.
- Keep Riddler trophies optional and reveal the grapple-gun model after pickup.
- Give short villains normal height, characters visible faces, Batman walking motion, substantial plot twists before villain fights, and drivable Batmobile controls.

## Decisions
- Retain the origin story cards and cave as the prologue, followed by playable encounters.
- Use chapter-specific objectives and named bosses, with a completion overlay to advance between chapters.

## Work State
### Completed
- Expanded the case-file story cards and added five optional cave trophies, a counter, and a grapple-gun pickup model.
- Added villain-specific boss visuals, combat objectives, chapter completion overlay, and chapter progression.
- Added 40 uniquely named playable chapter entries, including every requested villain.
- Updated chapter HUD labels, boss display, combat reset behavior, retry action, and final-story ending.
- Added Batman limb pivot groups and animated limbs during movement, resetting them at idle.
- Added shared enemy face details and villain-specific boss scaling.
- Added Batmobile enter/exit and driving controls, including steering, acceleration, boundaries, and wheel rotation.
- Added 40 chapter-specific plot twist dialogues in `chapterTwists`.

### Active
- Integrate `chapterTwists` into chapter introductions and/or pre-boss dialogue so the twists appear in gameplay.
- Verify syntax, `git diff --check`, and gameplay across the prologue and chapters; confirm Batmobile interaction and driving behavior.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Wire each chapter’s twist into its introduction or pre-boss dialogue.
2. Run syntax and diff checks, then test the prologue, movement, Batmobile controls, and chapter progression.
3. Fix any issues found during verification.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game scene, character and vehicle models, chapter data and dialogue, controls, combat, and progression UI.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; `index.html` is modified.
- Cave is the prologue; playable chapters are numbered 01–40.
- Batmobile interaction is through E when near the vehicle; W/S drive, A/D steer, and E exits.

183:   'The shopkeeper hid a ledger beneath the counter: Black Mask’s crew are collecting rents for a block that was condemned years ago, and the real target is the tenants’ deed archive.',

207:   'Croc is protecting a group of residents whose homes were condemned without relocation. The tunnel collapse is being triggered remotely to force them out before inspectors arrive.',
208:   'Hatter has left the clock stopped at the victims’ chosen time. The centerpiece is not a bomb but a projector; the real danger is the crew outside who will take them away again.',
209:   'The recovered cell is not enough to cure Nora, but Wayne Medical has found a stable treatment. Victor is stealing power to keep her alive until the doctors can reach her.',
210:   'Bane’s final strike targets the evacuation convoy, but his own crew has split: several have sent the route to dispatch because they refuse to attack civilians.',
211:   'The parade route is not wired with explosives. Joker’s crew has swapped the route signs to send the crowd toward an unsafe bridge, and the real bomb threat is a planted distraction.',

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Expand and polish the Batman game into a story with playable chapters, retaining the origin and cave prologue while improving characters, movement, and Batmobile driving.

## Requirements
- Keep the origin first, followed by playable chapters and villain encounters; story cards alone do not count as playable chapters.
- Include Joker, Bane, Riddler, Two-Face, Killer Croc, Mad Hatter, and Mr. Freeze.
- Keep Riddler trophies optional and reveal the grapple-gun model after pickup.
- Give short villains normal height, characters visible faces, Batman walking motion, substantial plot twists before villain fights, and drivable Batmobile controls.

## Decisions
- Retain the origin story cards and cave as the prologue, followed by playable encounters.
- Use chapter-specific objectives and named bosses, with a completion overlay to advance between chapters.
- Show each chapter’s twist during the boss-arrival dialogue.

## Work State
### Completed
- Expanded the case-file story cards and added five optional cave trophies, a counter, and a grapple-gun pickup model.
- Added villain-specific boss visuals, combat objectives, chapter completion overlay, and chapter progression.
- Added 40 uniquely named playable chapter entries, including every requested villain.
- Added 40 chapter-specific plot twists and wired each into boss-arrival dialogue.
- Updated chapter HUD labels, boss display, combat reset behavior, retry action, and final-story ending.
- Added Batman limb pivot groups and animated limbs during movement, resetting them at idle.
- Added shared enemy face details and villain-specific boss scaling.
- Added Batmobile enter/exit and driving controls, including steering, acceleration, boundaries, and wheel rotation.
- Confirmed 40 chapters and 40 twists; extracted the module script and passed `node --check`; `git diff --check` passed.

### Active
- Verify gameplay in a browser across the prologue, movement, Batmobile interaction/driving, and chapter progression.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Run browser gameplay checks for the cave prologue, optional trophies and grapple pickup, movement, Batmobile controls, and chapter progression.
2. Fix any issues found and rerun syntax and diff checks.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game scene, story and chapter data, dialogue, controls, combat, and progression UI.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; `index.html` is modified.
- Cave is the prologue; playable chapters are numbered 01–40.
- Batmobile interaction is through E when near the vehicle; W/S drive, A/D steer, and E exits.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Expand and polish the Batman game into a story with playable chapters, retaining the origin and cave prologue while improving characters, movement, and Batmobile driving.

## Requirements
- Keep the origin first, followed by playable chapters and villain encounters; story cards alone do not count as playable chapters.
- Include Joker, Bane, Riddler, Two-Face, Killer Croc, Mad Hatter, and Mr. Freeze.
- Keep Riddler trophies optional and reveal the grapple-gun model after pickup.
- Give short villains normal height, characters visible faces, Batman walking motion, substantial plot twists before villain fights, and drivable Batmobile controls.

## Decisions
- Retain the origin story cards and cave as the prologue, followed by playable encounters.
- Use chapter-specific objectives and named bosses, with a completion overlay to advance between chapters.
- Show each chapter’s twist during the boss-arrival dialogue.

## Work State
### Completed
- Expanded the case-file story cards and added five optional cave trophies, a counter, and a grapple-gun pickup model.
- Added villain-specific boss visuals, combat objectives, chapter completion overlay, and chapter progression.
- Added 40 uniquely named playable chapter entries, including every requested villain.
- Added 40 chapter-specific plot twists and wired each into boss-arrival dialogue.
- Updated chapter HUD labels, boss display, combat reset behavior, retry action, and final-story ending.
- Added Batman limb pivot groups and animated limbs during movement, resetting them at idle.
- Added shared enemy face details and villain-specific boss scaling.
- Added Batmobile enter/exit and driving controls, including steering, acceleration, boundaries, and wheel rotation.
- Browser checks confirmed the title and story cards render, the 40-card origin sequence advances into the cave prologue, cave dialogue can be dismissed, and player movement updates interaction prompts.
- Confirmed 40 playable chapters and 40 twists; extracted the module script and passed `node --check`; `git diff --check` passed.

### Active
- Finish browser gameplay checks for cave equipment and optional trophies, grapple-gun visibility, Batmobile interaction/driving, and chapter progression.
- Investigate the browser’s 404 for `/favicon.ico` if relevant; no application JavaScript errors were reported.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Continue browser checks in the cave, including the optional trophies, grapple-gun pickup model, and Batmobile enter/drive/exit.
2. Test elevator-to-chapter transition, boss-arrival twist dialogue, and chapter advancement.
3. Fix any issues found and rerun syntax and diff checks.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game scene, story and chapter data, dialogue, controls, combat, and progression UI.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; `index.html` is modified.
- Cave is the prologue; playable chapters are numbered 01–40.
- Batmobile interaction is through E when near the vehicle; W/S drive, A/D steer, and E exits.
- Browser is at `http://localhost:3002`; this port was already serving the game when the attempted Python server reported `OSError: [Errno 98] Address already in use`.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Expand and polish the Batman game into a story with playable chapters, retaining the origin and cave prologue while improving characters, movement, and Batmobile driving.

## Requirements
- Keep the origin first, followed by playable chapters and villain encounters; story cards alone do not count as playable chapters.
- Include Joker, Bane, Riddler, Two-Face, Killer Croc, Mad Hatter, and Mr. Freeze.
- Keep Riddler trophies optional and reveal the grapple-gun model after pickup.
- Give short villains normal height, characters visible faces, Batman walking motion, substantial plot twists before villain fights, and drivable Batmobile controls.

## Decisions
- Retain the origin story cards and cave as the prologue, followed by playable encounters.
- Use chapter-specific objectives and named bosses, with a completion overlay to advance between chapters.
- Show each chapter’s twist during the boss-arrival dialogue.

## Work State
### Completed
- Expanded the case-file story cards and added five optional cave trophies, a counter, and a grapple-gun pickup model.
- Added villain-specific boss visuals, combat objectives, chapter completion overlay, and chapter progression.
- Added 40 uniquely named playable chapter entries, including every requested villain.
- Added 40 chapter-specific plot twists and wired each into boss-arrival dialogue.
- Updated chapter HUD labels, boss display, combat reset behavior, retry action, and final-story ending.
- Added Batman limb pivot groups and animated limbs during movement, resetting them at idle.
- Added shared enemy face details and villain-specific boss scaling.
- Added Batmobile enter/exit and driving controls, including steering, acceleration, boundaries, and wheel rotation.
- Browser checks confirmed title/story rendering, advancement through all 40 origin cards into the cave, cave dialogue dismissal, movement prompts, collecting one optional trophy, grapple-gun pickup dialogue/toast, and Batmobile enter/drive/exit prompts.
- Confirmed 40 playable chapters and 40 twists; extracted the module script and passed `node --check`; `git diff --check` passed.

### Active
- Finish browser checks for visibility of the grapple-gun model after pickup, remaining optional trophies, and actual Batmobile movement.
- Test elevator-to-chapter transition, boss-arrival twist dialogue, and chapter advancement.
- Investigate the browser’s 404 for `/favicon.ico` if relevant.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Continue browser checks for grapple-gun visibility, optional trophies, and Batmobile movement.
2. Test the elevator transition, boss dialogue, and chapter advancement.
3. Fix any issues found and rerun syntax and diff checks.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game scene, story and chapter data, dialogue, controls, combat, and progression UI.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; `index.html` is modified.
- Cave is the prologue; playable chapters are numbered 01–40.
- Batmobile interaction is through E when near the vehicle; W/S drive, A/D steer, and E exits.
- Browser is at `http://localhost:3002`; the page loaded without application JavaScript errors, but reported a missing `/favicon.ico`.

playwright-cli - run playwright mcp commands from terminal

Usage: playwright-cli <command> [args] [options]
Usage: playwright-cli -s=<session> <command> [args] [options]

Core:
  open [url]                  open the browser
  attach [name]               attach to a running playwright browser
  close                       close the browser
  detach                      detach from an attached browser
  goto <url>                  navigate to a url
  type <text>                 type text into editable element
  click <target> [button]     perform click on a web page
  dblclick <target> [button]  perform double click on a web page
  fill <target> <text>        fill text into editable element
  drag <startTarget> <endTarget> perform drag and drop between two elements
  drop <target>               drop files or data onto an element
  hover <target>              hover over element on page
  select <target> <val>       select an option in a dropdown
  upload <files...>           upload one or multiple files
  check <target>              check a checkbox or radio button
  uncheck <target>            uncheck a checkbox or radio button
  snapshot [target]           capture page snapshot to obtain element ref
  find [text]                 search the page snapshot for text or a regexp, returning matching nodes with surrounding context (like search snippets)
  eval <func> [target]        evaluate javascript expression on page or element
  dialog-accept [prompt]      accept a dialog
  dialog-dismiss              dismiss a dialog
  resize <w> <h>              resize the browser window
  delete-data                 delete session data

Navigation:
  go-back                     go back to the previous page
  go-forward                  go forward to the next page
  reload                      reload the current page

Keyboard:
  press <key>                 press a key on the keyboard, `a`, `arrowleft`
  keydown <key>               press a key down on the keyboard
  keyup <key>                 press a key up on the keyboard

Mouse:
  mousemove <x> <y>           move mouse to a given position
  mousedown [button]          press mouse down
  mouseup [button]            press mouse up
  mousewheel <dx> <dy>        scroll mouse wheel

Save as:
  screenshot [target]         screenshot of the current page or element
  pdf                         save page as pdf

Tabs:
  tab-list                    list all tabs
  tab-new [url]               create a new tab
  tab-close [index]           close a browser tab
  tab-select <index>          select a browser tab

Storage:
  state-load <filename>       loads browser storage (authentication) state from a file
  state-save [filename]       saves the current storage (authentication) state to a file
  cookie-list                 list all cookies (optionally filtered by domain/path)
  cookie-get <name>           get a specific cookie by name
  cookie-set <name> <value>   set a cookie with optional flags
  cookie-delete <name>        delete a specific cookie
  cookie-clear                clear all cookies
  localstorage-list           list all localstorage key-value pairs
  localstorage-get <key>      get a localstorage item by key
  localstorage-set <key> <value> set a localstorage item
  localstorage-delete <key>   delete a localstorage item
  localstorage-clear          clear all localstorage
  sessionstorage-list         list all sessionstorage key-value pairs
  sessionstorage-get <key>    get a sessionstorage item by key
  sessionstorage-set <key> <value> set a sessionstorage item
  sessionstorage-delete <key> delete a sessionstorage item
  sessionstorage-clear        clear all sessionstorage

Network:
  requests                    list all network requests since loading the page. each request is numbered for use with the `request` command.
  request <index>             show full details (headers, body, response) of a single network request by its number from the `requests` command.
  request-headers <index>     print only the request headers for a single network request by its number from the `requests` command.
  request-body <index>        print only the request body for a single network request by its number from the `requests` command.
  response-headers <index>    print only the response headers for a single network request by its number from the `requests` command.
  response-body <index>       print the response body for a single network request by its number from the `requests` command. textual bodies are inlined; binary bodies are saved to a file and the path is printed.
  route <pattern>             mock network requests matching a url pattern
  route-list                  list all active network routes
  unroute [pattern]           remove routes matching a pattern (or all routes)
  network-state-set <state>   set the browser network state to online or offline

DevTools:
  console [min-level]         list console messages
  run-code [code]             run playwright code snippet
  recording-start             start recording user actions
  recording-stop              stop recording user actions and print them as playwright code
  tracing-start               start trace recording
  tracing-stop                stop trace recording
  video-start [filename]      start video recording
  video-stop                  stop video recording
  video-chapter <title>       add a chapter marker to the video recording
  video-show-actions          annotate subsequent cli/mcp actions on the page with a callout that names the action and highlights the target element
  video-hide-actions          stop annotating actions performed on the page
  show                        show playwright dashboard
  pause-at <location>         run the test up to a specific location and pause there
  resume                      resume the test execution
  step-over                   step over the next call in the test
  generate-locator <target>   generate a playwright locator for the given element
  highlight [target]          show (or with --hide, remove) a highlight overlay for an element; `--hide` without a target hides all page highlights.

Install:
  install                     initialize workspace
  install-browser [browser]   install browser

Browser sessions:
  list                        list browser sessions
  close-all                   close all browser sessions
  kill-all                    forcefully kill all browser sessions (for stale/zombie processes)

Global options:
  --help [command]            print help
  --json                      output response as JSON
  --raw                       output only the result value, without status and code
  --version                   print version

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Expand and polish the Batman game into a story with playable chapters, retaining the origin and cave prologue while improving characters, movement, and Batmobile driving.

## Requirements
- Keep the origin first, followed by playable chapters and villain encounters; story cards alone do not count as playable chapters.
- Include Joker, Bane, Riddler, Two-Face, Killer Croc, Mad Hatter, and Mr. Freeze.
- Keep Riddler trophies optional and reveal the grapple-gun model after pickup.
- Give short villains normal height, characters visible faces, Batman walking motion, substantial plot twists before villain fights, and drivable Batmobile controls.

## Decisions
- Retain the origin story cards and cave as the prologue, followed by playable encounters.
- Use chapter-specific objectives and named bosses, with a completion overlay to advance between chapters.
- Show each chapter’s twist during the boss-arrival dialogue.

## Work State
### Completed
- Expanded the case-file story cards and added five optional cave trophies, a counter, and a grapple-gun pickup model.
- Added villain-specific boss visuals, combat objectives, chapter completion overlay, and chapter progression.
- Added 40 uniquely named playable chapter entries, including every requested villain, and wired 40 chapter twists into boss-arrival dialogue.
- Updated chapter HUD labels, boss display, combat reset behavior, retry action, and final-story ending.
- Added Batman limb pivots and walking animation, shared enemy face details, and villain-specific boss scaling.
- Added Batmobile enter/exit and driving controls, including steering, acceleration, boundaries, and wheel rotation.
- Browser checks confirmed story advancement into the cave, dialogue dismissal, and Batmobile proximity prompt; `git diff --check` passed.
- `index.html` remains modified and uncommitted.

### Active
- Continue browser verification of grapple-gun visibility after pickup, optional trophies, and actual Batmobile movement.
- Test elevator-to-chapter transition, boss-arrival twist dialogue, and chapter advancement.

### Blocked
- Browser movement testing has been unreliable: input checks showed prompts changing, but not consistently, and the grapple-gun pickup has not yet been confirmed. No confirmed code blocker.

## Next Move
1. Continue browser checks for grapple-gun visibility, optional trophy collection, and actual Batmobile movement.
2. Test elevator transition, boss twist dialogue, and chapter advancement; fix issues found.
3. Rerun syntax and diff checks.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game scene, story and chapter data, dialogue, controls, combat, and progression UI.

## Important Context
- Cave is the prologue; playable chapters are numbered 01–40.
- Batmobile interaction uses E when near the vehicle; W/S drive, A/D steer, and E exits.
- Browser is at `http://localhost:3002`; there have been no application JavaScript console errors in checks so far.
- Some browser tests used DOM-synthetic input that did not reliably verify game movement or dialogue state.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Expand and polish the Batman game into a story with playable chapters, retaining the origin and cave prologue while improving characters, movement, and Batmobile driving.

## Requirements
- Keep the origin first, followed by playable chapters and villain encounters; story cards alone do not count as playable chapters.
- Include Joker, Bane, Riddler, Two-Face, Killer Croc, Mad Hatter, and Mr. Freeze.
- Keep Riddler trophies optional and reveal the grapple-gun model after pickup.
- Give short villains normal height, characters visible faces, Batman walking motion, substantial plot twists before villain fights, and drivable Batmobile controls.

## Decisions
- Retain the origin story cards and cave as the prologue, followed by playable encounters.
- Use chapter-specific objectives and named bosses, with a completion overlay to advance between chapters.
- Show each chapter’s twist during the boss-arrival dialogue.

## Work State
### Completed
- Expanded the case-file story cards and added five optional cave trophies, a counter, and a grapple-gun pickup model.
- Added villain-specific boss visuals, combat objectives, chapter completion overlay, and chapter progression.
- Added 40 uniquely named playable chapter entries, including every requested villain, and wired 40 chapter twists into boss-arrival dialogue.
- Updated chapter HUD labels, boss display, combat reset behavior, retry action, and final-story ending.
- Added Batman limb pivots and walking animation, shared enemy face details, and villain-specific boss scaling.
- Added Batmobile enter/exit and driving controls, including steering, acceleration, boundaries, and wheel rotation.
- Browser checks confirmed story advancement into the cave, dialogue dismissal, and Batmobile proximity prompt; no application JavaScript console errors were reported.
- `git diff --check` passed.

### Active
- Continue browser verification of grapple-gun visibility after pickup, optional trophy collection, Batmobile movement, and elevator-to-chapter transition.
- Test boss-arrival twist dialogue and chapter advancement; fix issues found.

### Blocked
- Browser movement and interaction checks remain inconsistent: the Batmobile proximity prompt appeared, but pressing E did not show a clear state change; grapple pickup and actual driving remain unconfirmed.

## Next Move
1. Continue browser checks for grapple-gun visibility, optional trophy collection, Batmobile enter/drive/exit, and elevator transition.
2. Verify boss-arrival twist dialogue and chapter advancement; fix any issues.
3. Rerun syntax and diff checks.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game scene, story and chapter data, dialogue, controls, combat, and progression UI.

## Important Context
- Cave is the prologue; playable chapters are numbered 01–40.
- Batmobile interaction uses E when near the vehicle; W/S drive, A/D steer, and E exits.
- Browser is at `http://localhost:3002`.
- `index.html` remains modified and uncommitted.

  state-save [filename]       saves the current storage (authentication) state to a file

  request-headers <index>     print only the request headers for a single network request by its number from the `requests` command.
  request-body <index>        print only the request body for a single network request by its number from the `requests` command.
  response-headers <index>    print only the response headers for a single network request by its number from the `requests` command.

  route <pattern>             mock network requests matching a url pattern
  route-list                  list all active network routes

content.text:
playwright-cli - run playwright mcp commands from terminal

Usage: playwright-cli <command> [args] [options]
Usage: playwright-cli -s=<session> <command> [args] [options]

Core:
  open [url]                  open the browser
  attach [name]               attach to a running playwright browser
  close                       close the browser
  detach                      detach from an attached browser
  goto <url>                  navigate to a url
  type <text>                 type text into editable element
  click <target> [button]     perform click on a web page
  dblclick <target> [button]  perform double click on a web page
  fill <target> <text>        fill text into editable element
  drag <startTarget> <endTarget> perform drag and drop between two elements
  drop <target>               drop files or data onto an element
  hover <target>              hover over element on page
  select <target> <val>       select an option in a dropdown
  upload <files...>           upload one or multiple files
  check <target>              check a checkbox or radio button
  uncheck <target>            uncheck a checkbox or radio button
  snapshot [target]           capture page snapshot to obtain element ref
  find [text]                 search the page snapshot for text or a regexp, returning matching nodes with surrounding context (like search snippets)
  eval <func> [target]        evaluate javascript expression on page or element
  dialog-accept [prompt]      accept a dialog
  dialog-dismiss              dismiss a dialog
  resize <w> <h>              resize the browser window
  delete-data                 delete session data

Navigation:
  go-back                     go back to the previous page
  go-forward                  go forward to the next page
  reload                      reload the current page

Keyboard:
  press <key>                 press a key on the keyboard, `a`, `arrowleft`
  keydown <key>               press a key down on the keyboard
  keyup <key>                 press a key up on the keyboard

Mouse:
  mousemove <x> <y>           move mouse to a given position
  mousedown [button]          press mouse down
  mouseup [button]            press mouse up
  mousewheel <dx> <dy>        scroll mouse wheel

Save as:
  screenshot [target]         screenshot of the current page or element
  pdf                         save page as pdf

Tabs:
  tab-list                    list all tabs
  tab-new [url]               create a new tab
  tab-close [index]           close a browser tab
  tab-select <index>          select a browser tab

Storage:
  state-load <filename>       loads browser storage (authentication) state from a file
  state-save [filename]       saves the current storage (authentication) state to a file
  cookie-list                 list all cookies (optionally filtered by domain/path)
  cookie-get <name>           get a specific cookie by name
  cookie-set <name> <value>   set a cookie with optional flags
  cookie-delete <name>        delete a specific cookie
  cookie-clear                clear all cookies
  localstorage-list           list all localstorage key-value pairs
  localstorage-get <key>      get a localstorage item by key
  localstorage-set <key> <value> set a localstorage item
  localstorage-delete <key>   delete a localstorage item
  localstorage-clear          clear all localstorage
  sessionstorage-list         list all sessionstorage key-value pairs
  sessionstorage-get <key>    get a sessionstorage item by key
  sessionstorage-set <key> <value> set a sessionstorage item
  sessionstorage-delete <key> delete a sessionstorage item
  sessionstorage-clear        clear all sessionstorage

Network:
  requests                    list all network requests since loading the page. each request is numbered for use with the `request` command.
  request <index>             show full details (headers, body, response) of a single network request by its number from the `requests` command.
  request-headers <index>     print only the request headers for a single network request by its number from the `requests` command.
  request-body <index>        print only the request body for a single network request by its number from the `requests` command.
  response-headers <index>    print only the response headers for a single network request by its number from the `requests` command.
  response-body <index>       print the response body for a single network request by its number from the `requests` command. textual bodies are inlined; binary bodies are saved to a file and the path is printed.
  route <pattern>             mock network requests matching a url pattern
  route-list                  list all active network routes
  unroute [pattern]           remove routes matching a pattern (or all routes)
  network-state-set <state>   set the browser network state to online or offline

DevTools:
  console [min-level]         list console messages
  run-code [code]             run playwright code snippet
  recording-start             start recording user actions
  recording-stop              stop recording user actions and print them as playwright code
  tracing-start               start trace recording
  tracing-stop                stop trace recording
  video-start [filename]      start video recording
  video-stop                  stop video recording
  video-chapter <title>       add a chapter marker to the video recording
  video-show-actions          annotate subsequent cli/mcp actions on the page with a callout that names the action and highlights the target element
  video-hide-actions          stop annotating actions performed on the page
  show                        show playwright dashboard
  pause-at <location>         run the test up to a specific location and pause there
  resume                      resume the test execution
  step-over                   step over the next call in the test
  generate-locator <target>   generate a playwright locator for the given element
  highlight [target]          show (or with --hide, remove) a highlight overlay for an element; `--hide` without a target hides all page highlights.

Install:
  install                     initialize workspace
  install-browser [browser]   install browser

Browser sessions:
  list                        list browser sessions
  close-all                   close all browser sessions
  kill-all                    forcefully kill all browser sessions (for stale/zombie processes)

Global options:
  --help [command]            print help
  --json                      output response as JSON
  --raw                       output only the result value, without status and code
  --version                   print version
